verdict.rationale: Religare is demerging its entire financial services business — SME/MSME lending (Religare Finvest), retail broking plus e-governance (Religare Broking and its subsidiary Religare Digital Solutions), affordable housing finance (Religare Housing Development Finance, already an RFL subsidiary), and the related investment and ancillary/support activities — out of the listed holdco REL into RFL, which will itself be listed, leaving REL as a pure-play holder of its 63.2% stake in Care Health Insurance; REL shareholders get 1 RFL share for every REL share, and RFL's pre-scheme capital held by REL is cancelled so RFL's shareholding mirrors REL's. Management framed it as three converging conditions rather than a reaction to distress: the Burman Group's completed takeover as promoters (open offer concluded Feb 2025, board reconstituted July 2025, promoters at 29.75% fully diluted in Feb 2026 and ~30.3% by May 2026 after ~4% of open-market buying, heading to ~34% on warrant conversion), the INR1,500 crore preferential warrant raise subscribed 50:50 by the Burmans and marquee investors (earmarked INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, INR75 crore to repay REL's own debt and INR375 crore general corporate purpose), and the fact that the businesses had reached an inflection point where "each business also operates with different capital requirements, risk frameworks, manpower talent and growth trajectories." The stated problems it solves are a conglomerate structure in which insurance (FY26 GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore on 'n' basis, 19.7% retail SAHI share) drowns out a tiny financial services segment (FY25 demerged-undertaking turnover of only INR457.29 crore, 6.2% of consolidated revenue), investors who cannot value the two halves, and management bandwidth: the scheme's four pillars are streamlined focus/simplified structure, value unlocking plus targeted capital raising through a separate RFL listing, dedicated leadership with sector-specific talent and performance-linked rewards, and risk/compliance frameworks tailored to each segment. The financial services side is being restarted from a cleaned-up base — RFL is debt-free with all legacy promoter-era diversion issues provided or written off (including the full INR750 crore Lakshmi Vilas Bank FD), RBI's Corrective Action Plan lifted in July 2025 and bank fraud tags removed, leaving ~INR591 crore cash, ~INR900 crore net worth, 261% CRAR, NOF of INR821 crore and only a ~INR60 crore core SME book — so Arjun Lamba tied the demerger directly to scaling: "Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this." Who asked for it: shareholders and analysts had been pressing since the first call back in Nov 2025 (Vikas Shrivastav on demerging Care and removing the holdco discount, Dixit Doshi on IPO vs demerger of Care), and after the announcement nearly every questioner — Umang Shah, Adarsh, Hitaindra Pradhan, Ravi Purohit, Niharika Karnani, Sarvesh Gupta — argued the value sits in Care and demanded a reverse merger giving direct Care shares, citing the Max Financial precedent. Management conceded the point but said IRDAI's 25–26% promoter requirement cannot be met while the Burmans' look-through stake in Care is only ~18–19%, so this was "the first step in that direction," done after evaluating structural alternatives with leading advisors; Lamba refused to amend the scheme and would not commit to a timeline for a second one. Execution has since run into the regulator: exchanges gave no-objection/no-adverse-observation letters on 7 July 2026, but on 6–7 August 2026 RBI informed REL and RFL that their application for no-objection/prior approval "has not been acceded to," and the companies said they would engage further with the regulator.
verdict.evolution: On the Nov 2025 call (Q2/H1 FY26, the first investor call after the Burman takeover) there was no plan — Vikas Shrivastav asked directly what the structure would look like in two years and whether Care would be demerged from the holdco, and CFO Pratul Gupta would only say the board was evaluating options and wanted to make the businesses "larger, better, stronger" before any capital-market action, while Dixit Doshi asked whether Care would be IPO'd or demerged. A Moneycontrol report on 3 Feb 2026 that REL would demerge and list Care drew an exchange query, which REL denied as a disclosable event; eleven days later, on 14 Feb 2026, the REL and RFL boards approved the scheme — and the Feb 2026 call (16 Feb) was where Gupta laid out the full rationale, the four pillars, the 1:1 ratio, the 15–18 month timetable and a Q1 FY28 RFL listing, while every analyst pushed back that Care, not financial services, should have been separated. By the May 2026 call (13 May, Q4/FY26) the framing had shifted from Gupta's structural logic to Executive Director Arjun Lamba's: separating FS from insurance was "number one," the promoters had bought ~4% more stock toward the IRDAI threshold, and he declined to amend the scheme while leaving a later reverse merger of Care open "at an appropriate stage." The 7 July 2026 exchange observation letters cleared the way, but the 7 Aug 2026 filings disclosed RBI had refused to accede to the application, leaving the scheme stalled pending further engagement.

points.point: Asked outright about demerging Care and the other subsidiaries from the holdco and about removing the holdco discount, Pratul Gupta said nothing was decided — the board was weighing options and wanted to strengthen the businesses first, after the INR1,500 crore raise, before any capital-market action.
points.quote: On the second question about how the structure will look like in some future time, what I can very clearly assure you is that the management and the Board is evaluating various options which can add value to the shareholders.

points.point: Investors were already framing the choice as Care IPO versus demerger; Dixit Doshi asked it explicitly alongside questions on NBFC yields, showing the separation idea originated with shareholders rather than management.
points.quote: And in terms of your initial comments on the value unlocking, if you can just touch upon whether we will be looking for an IPO for the care health business or we will be better off with the de -merger of the business?

points.point: Gupta presented the demerger as a strategic imperative rather than a housekeeping exercise, announced two days after the REL and RFL boards approved it on 14 Feb 2026.
points.quote: It is a strategic imperati ve step designed to unlock shareholder value, create business clarity and position the resulting entities for sustained long -term growth.

points.point: The trigger was three converging conditions — the Burman takeover as promoters, the INR1,500 crore warrant raise covering funding needs for the foreseeable future, and the businesses reaching a scale that demands specialised focus.
points.quote: Each business also operates with different capital requirements, risk frameworks, manpower talent and growth trajectories.

points.point: Mechanics: lending, broking and ancillary support services move from REL to RFL on a going-concern basis, the Care stake stays in REL, RFL issues one share per REL share and then lists, with a 15–18 month process ending in Q1 FY28.
points.quote: The lending, broking and ancillary support services held under REL shall be demer ged into RFL on a going concern basis. The investment in CARE shall continue to be retained in REL.

points.point: A separate RFL listing is meant to unlock value, widen investor participation and let that business raise its own capital — the second of four stated pillars.
points.quote: The independent listing of RFL is expected to unlock shareholder value and enhance investor participation.

points.point: Analysts attacked the design immediately: Umang Shah argued demerging Care directly would have removed the holdco discount on the asset that carries most of the value.
points.quote: I'm a bit puzzled why we chose to demerge financial services and not CARE directly?

points.point: Gupta positioned this as stage one of a longer restructuring, with a Care reverse merger possible later once unspecified milestones and minimum-shareholding thresholds are met.
points.quote: Well, I think this is -- as I mentioned, this is the first step in that direction.

points.point: The binding constraint on a Care reverse merger is the IRDAI promoter-shareholding rule against a Burman look-through stake in Care of only ~18–19%, which Gupta confirmed when Vikas Srivastava spelled out the law.
points.quote: So you are right in terms of the fact that the look - through shareholding of the promoter group today in CARE is at around 18% to 19%.

points.point: Management said the structure was chosen after a full review of alternatives with external advisors, and promised no operational, customer or employee disruption during implementation.
points.quote: This has resulted after comprehensive evalu ation of various structural alternatives which were discussed with leading advisors.

points.point: Arjun Lamba restated the core purpose as separating financial services from insurance to give shareholders a clean, understandable structure and management a single focus, while acknowledging the holdco-discount complaint.
points.quote: And for us, number one has been to separate the FS business from the insurance business and to provide a clean structure so that the shareholders can understand, th e management can be very focused in doing what they have to do.

points.point: Lamba linked the demerger to the capital allocation plan — INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, ~INR375 crore general corporate purpose, with RFL needing none given ~INR900–1,000 crore net worth and ~INR600 crore cash.
points.quote: Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this.

points.point: Pressed by Vikas Srivastava on whether the scheme could be amended to fold Care in once the promoters reach 26%, Lamba ruled out amending it but left a subsequent scheme open.
points.quote: No, I'll answer your last question first. We don't want to amend the scheme.

points.point: Lamba conceded the value is concentrated in Care and said the separation is intended to create value in the other entity too, as promoters moved from ~26% toward ~34% diluted.
points.quote: Yes, we understand that the value is in Care. We are cognizant of that. That's why we are separating the entities, creating clear paths, and we hope to create value in the other entity as well

points.point: The 14 Feb 2026 filing states the demerged undertaking is all of REL's financial services activity — lending, broking, investment and ancillary/support services — explicitly excluding the retained insurance business, i.e. the Care Health shareholding.
points.quote: Provided that, the Demerged Undertaking shall exclude the Remaining Business ( as defined in the Scheme ) compris ing of all the units, divisions, undertakings, assets and liabilities in relation to the Demerged Company’s insurance business, comprising of its investment and shareholding in Care Health Insurance Limited .

points.point: The scheme quantifies how small the demerged half is: FY25 turnover of INR457.29 crore on a consolidated basis, just 6.2% of REL's consolidated turnover.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31  March , 202 5 was INR 457.29 Crores on a consolidated basis  representing 6.2% of the total consolidated turnover of the Company for the year ended 31 March , 202 5.

points.point: Stated rationale includes that the two businesses face different competition and attract different investors, partners and lenders, and that a separately listed vehicle enables sector-focused talent and growth opportunities.
points.quote: The nature and competition involved in the businesses comprising of the Demerged Undertaking is distinct from the other businesses and it is capable of attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.

points.point: The press release lists four objectives — streamlining businesses, listing financial services, focused management with performance mapped to each business, and segment-tailored risk and compliance frameworks — with 1:1 mirror shareholding in RFL and listing targeted for Q1 FY28.
points.quote: Focused management attention:  Enable mapping of employee p erformance and rewards to respective business outcomes, and facilitate attraction and retention of sector -specific talent and resources.

points.point: SEBI's comments routed through the NSE observation letter of 7 July 2026 require REL to disclose the need for the demerger, cost-benefit analysis, risks and the RBI approval position to shareholders — i.e. the rationale was not yet fully documented for them.
points.quote: Need for demerger, rationale of the scheme, synergies of  business of the entities involved in the scheme, impact of the scheme on the shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the s cheme.

points.point: Execution setback: after exchange no-objections on 7 July 2026, RBI declined the no-objection/prior-approval applications of both REL and RFL in letters dated 6 and 7 August 2026, and the companies said they would go back to the regulator.
points.quote: The Company has received a letter dated August 6, 2026 , from the RBI, conveying that the application has been examined and that the request has not been acceded to .

verdict.what_management_expects: REL becomes a pure-play health insurance holdco around Care (GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore 'n' basis, combined ratio heading from 101.4% to ~100% in two years on operating leverage, 18–24% growth). RFL becomes an integrated, separately listed financial services platform — debt-free, ~INR900 crore net worth, ~INR591 crore cash, 261% CRAR — able to leverage to industry norms, raise targeted capital, hire sector-specific leadership on performance-linked rewards, run tailored risk frameworks, and unlock value via mirror 1:1 listing.
verdict.gaps: No cost-benefit or synergy quantification, no RFL valuation or AUM/ROE targets, no holdco-discount fix or Care reverse-merger timeline, no stated path to IRDAI's 26%, and no RBI-rejection reasoning.

Segment revenue is stated as 'before inter-segment revenue adjustments' (i.e. includes inter-segment), per footnote on Presentation May 2026 p.10. No segment-level PAT is disclosed. Annual reports instead split this business into 'Investment and Financing Activities' and 'Broking Related Activities' (₹ lakhs) and report 'Segment Results', so they carry no single 'Financial Services' line.

verdict.rationale: This is not a sale but a three-way split by demerger: a Scheme of Arrangement approved by MSL's board (first on 22 May 2026, then re-approved 7 October 2026 with an Appointed Date of 1 October 2026) carves two 'Demerged Undertakings' out of Maharashtra Seamless into two wholly owned subsidiaries that will themselves be listed on BSE and NSE. Demerged Undertaking 1 — the Mangaon, Maharashtra seamless pipe plant (125,000 MTPA) plus the 10 MW captive solar plant at Beed — goes to MSL Seamless Tubes Limited (MSTL); Demerged Undertaking 2 — the Narketpally, Telangana seamless mill (200,000 MTPA), the Khetusar (20 MW) and Pokhran (5 MW) solar plants in Rajasthan, and the rig Jindal Explorer — goes to United Seamless Limited (USL), i.e. the asset base MSL bought out of IBC as United Seamless Tubulaar for INR477 crores plus INR73 crores of reactivation capex. On FY2025-26 operational turnover the split is Undertaking 1 INR793 crores (16.98%), Undertaking 2 INR693 crores (14.84%) and the residual company (Nagothane pipes, ERW, treasury) INR3,185 crores (68.18%) of INR4,671 crores. The board's stated reasons are that the undertakings have 'distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration' — specifically three different mill technologies, CPE at Nagothane, MPM at Mangaon and FQM at Telangana, each needing its own modernization and technical expertise — so each should run as a focused, independently reported vertical. It also says manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy have 'different capital intensity and funding requirements', so splitting them allows better assessment of capital needs and more flexibility for expansion; the renewable plants are attached to the mills they can power; and the rig business, long described on calls as outside the core, is segregated because it has 'distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business'. No cash changes hands: shareholders get 1 share of INR5 in each resulting company for every 5 MSL shares, producing the same proportionate holding (promoter ~70.30%, public ~29.70%, 2,67,99,850 shares in each), which the filing calls 'value neutral'; creditor liabilities are neither reduced nor extinguished and travel with each undertaking. Notably, the nine earnings calls supplied — including Feb 2026, three months before the first board approval — contain no mention of a demerger at all; the only antecedents are repeated investor pressure to exit the rig and one shareholder's demand to split the company, and management's standing answer that it would continue 'in the steel pipe segment only' and that exit was 'for the Board to decide'.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced only as a rig exit: on the Feb 2024 call (30 Jan 2024) Chairman D.P. Jindal said of staying in rigs 'we have to take the appropriate decision at the right time', and on the Nov 2024 call (29 Oct 2024) an investor asked directly about demerging or selling the rig, to which management said it was something 'we want to do, but it is subject to Board approval'. Pressure widened over the next year: on the Feb 2025 call (28 Jan 2025) management personally agreed the rig-to-Jindal-Drilling structure 'doesn't look in line' with its governance clean-up, on the Jun 2025 call (27 May 2025) it confirmed 'there was a view of getting out of the rig business' with no board update, and on the Aug 2025 call (31 July 2025) a shareholder explicitly asked management to 'divide the company in two parts' — a holding company and a seamless company — and got only 'I don't have anything to add'. By the Nov 2025 call (5 Nov 2025) there was still 'no update on the proposal', and the Feb 2026 call (29 Jan 2026) discussed only cash conservation, treasury and a hunt for distressed acquisitions. The actual plan then appeared without any call commentary: board approval 22 May 2026, a 15 June 2026 notice that the Scheme was 'under further review', and a revised, re-approved Scheme on 7 October 2026 that widened it from a rig/holding split into a full three-way break-up of the three mills by technology, with 'related assets and liabilities' tightened to 'specified assets and liabilities' and 'mirror shareholding' restated as 'same proportionate shareholding'.

points.point: Two undertakings are carved out into two wholly owned subsidiaries, MSL Seamless Tubes Limited and United Seamless Limited, both to be listed, with an Appointed Date of 1 October 2026; the Mangaon 125,000 MTPA mill and the 10 MW Beed captive solar plant form Undertaking 1.
points.quote: Demerged Undertaking 1: Seamless pipe manufacturing business of the Demerged Company located at Mangaon, Maharashtra (125,000 MTPA), captive solar power plant at Beed, Maharashtra (10 MW), along with the specified assets and liabilities of Demerged Undertaking 1.

points.point: Undertaking 2 bundles the Telangana (Narketpally) 200,000 MTPA mill with the Rajasthan solar plants and the rig Jindal Explorer into United Seamless Limited — effectively re-separating the ex-United Seamless Tubulaar asset base and the rig in one entity.
points.quote: Demerged Undertaking 2: Seamless pipe manufacturing facility of the Demerged Company located at Narketpally, Telangana (200,000 MTPA), solar power plants at Khetusar (20 MW) & Pokhran (5MW) in Rajasthan, rig Jindal Explorer along with the specified assets and liabilities of Demerged Undertaking 2.

points.point: The headline justification is that one company holds businesses with nothing in common operationally — different geographies, products, technologies, customers and logistics — so each should be managed separately.
points.quote: The said undertakings having distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration, commercial considerations and growth opportunities.

points.point: The most concrete operating reason given is that the three mills run on three different pipe-making technologies, each needing its own specialised management and modernization programme — which maps exactly onto the three-way split.
points.quote: The manufacturing facilities operate on different technological platforms, including CPE technology at Nagothane, MPM technology at Mangaon and FQM technology at Telangana, each requiring specialized operational management, modernization initiatives and technical expertise.

points.point: Capital allocation is cited: pipes, drilling and renewables have different capital intensity, so separation is meant to let each assess and fund its own needs — relevant given the stalled INR852 crore capex plan and the INR350 crore Nagothane hot-mill upgrade never started.
points.quote: Efficient Capital Allocation: The manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy businesses have different capital intensity and funding requirements.

points.point: The rig is singled out for segregation on the grounds that it is commercially unlike pipe manufacturing — the same objection investors had raised on calls for two years.
points.quote: Focused Development of Rig Operations: The rig business has distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business.

points.point: The renewable plants are deliberately attached to the mills they sit beside rather than kept central, framed as energy-management efficiency and sustainability support for each business.
points.quote: The renewable power assets proposed to be transferred along with the respective undertakings are expected to provide better operational alignment, energy management efficiencies and support sustainability initiatives of the corresponding businesses.

points.point: Separate financial and operational reporting per entity is itself presented as a benefit — transparency and performance evaluation — which speaks to the calls where management refused to give product-wise or mill-wise margins.
points.quote: Improved Transparency and Value Creation: The proposed demerger would result in creation of focused business entities with independent financial and operational reporting, thereby enhancing transparency, improving performance evaluation and facilitating long-term value creation for stakeholders.

points.point: No cash is paid; shareholders receive 1 INR5 share in each resulting company per 5 MSL shares, giving identical proportionate ownership (promoter 70.3008%, public 29.6992%, 2,67,99,850 shares each) and, the board says, value neutrality.
points.quote: The above share exchange ratios shall ensure same proportionate shareholding structure of Resulting Company 1 and Resulting Company 2 with Demerged Company and hence Scheme shall be value neutral to the Demerged Company's shareholders.

points.point: Lenders are explicitly left untouched: no arrangement or compromise with creditors, liabilities travelling with each undertaking — i.e. the split is not presented as lender-driven or a debt restructuring.
points.quote: The liabilities towards the creditors of the Demerged Company and/or the Resulting Companies under the Scheme are neither being reduced nor being extinguished and the liabilities pertaining to the respective undertakings shall be assumed and discharged by the respective Resulting Companies in the ordinary course of business.

points.point: The plan was not stable: approved 22 May 2026, pulled back for review on 15 June 2026, and re-approved only on 7 October 2026 with tightened wording ('specified' rather than 'related' assets, 'same proportionate' rather than 'mirror' shareholding) and slightly revised indicative share counts (promoter 70.2784% to 70.3008%).
points.quote: This is further to the intimation dated 22nd May, 2026, about the approval of the Scheme of Arrangement by the Board of Directors of the Company, we have to inform you that the said Scheme is under further review and would be placed before any subsequent Board Meeting for its approval and would be submitted to Stock Exchanges thereafter.

points.point: The first hint of any separation was about the rig: asked whether MSL would keep two verticals, the Chairman declined to commit, while noting day rates had risen (~$40,000/day, expecting a new contract above $80,000).
points.quote: Well, we have to take the appropriate decision at the right time.

points.point: An investor asked outright about demerging or selling the rig business post-May 2025; management confirmed intent but no board discussion and no valuation expectation.
points.quote: It is something which we want to do, but it is subject to Board approval.

points.point: After an investor said the rig arrangement (MSL renting the rig to group company Jindal Drilling, which sub-contracts to ONGC) looked out of line with MSL's governance clean-up, management personally agreed and promised a communication once board approvals came.
points.quote: You are right, and I personally agree with you, but once suitable decisions and Board approvals are received, we will send communication on this.

points.point: Management confirmed a rig exit had been contemplated but that the board had given no update, while re-committing to pipes only — the rig had just been recontracted to Jindal Drilling at ~$35,000/day L1, with MSL to get ~$17,000-18,000/day.
points.quote: There was a view of getting out of the rig business, but we've not received any update from the Board in the Board meeting, which concluded yesterday.

points.point: A five-year shareholder explicitly demanded the company be split so investors could choose the pipe business over the treasury/holding activity, arguing the merged picture was unclear; management offered no response.
points.quote: Either divide the company in two parts. One should be a holding company, one should be a seamless company.

points.point: Six months before board approval, an analyst asked specifically about getting the Jindal Explorer rig off the books and was told there was no update, with the rig about to start a new ONGC contract.
points.quote: There is no update on the proposal that you mentioned.

points.point: On the last call before the first board approval, management described the future as cash conservation and opportunistic distressed acquisitions, with no mention of any restructuring, while defending the INR3,500 crore treasury against shareholders noting ~50% of market cap was cash.
points.quote: We are conserving cash as of now and we are on the lookout for any inorganic opportunity that may arise, but that inorganic opportunity should be at a cost level at which we are comfortable.

points.point: The same call set out the economics of the Telangana asset that now forms United Seamless Limited: INR477 crores purchase plus INR73 crores reactivation, INR100-200 crores of EBITDA a year, and ~INR375 crores of tax saved from USTPL's INR1,500 crore-plus accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation.
points.quote: We acquired it for INR477 crores, and we invested an additional INR73 crores to reactivate the mill.

verdict.what_management_expects: Per the Scheme only: each mill run as a focused vertical with dedicated management and technology-specific modernization; sharper assessment and deployment of capital across pipes, drilling and renewables, with more flexibility for expansion; solar assets aligned to the mills they serve; the rig managed on its own terms; independent reporting improving transparency and performance evaluation; identical proportionate shareholding, so value-neutral. No margin, cost, ROCE or valuation figures were given.
verdict.gaps: No call ever mentioned it. Silent on where the ~INR3,500 crore treasury, debt, ERW and premium-connections subsidiary sit, on margins, valuation, lost shared overheads, and NCLT timing.

verdict.segment_name: Steel Pipes & Tubes (standalone/consolidated segment reporting); in the quarterly presentations split as "Seamless" and "ERW". The pages carry no line item labelled MSL Seamless Tubes Limited or Demerged Undertaking 1/2.
verdict.measure_notes: Annual operating_profit = "Segment Results" from Ind AS 108 segment note (PBIT, i.e. before finance costs and tax, after depreciation); Profit Before Tax for Steel Pipes & Tubes is 1,034.89 (FY24), 740.88 (FY25), 520.44 (FY26) — FY26 after exceptional items of 3.04. Steel Pipes & Tubes reports nil inter-segment sales, so segment revenue is external (only Power–Electricity carries inter-segment sales). Quarterly figure is EBITDA (pre-depreciation) for the Seamless business only, from the presentation's Operational & Financial Performance slide; ERW EBITDA is given separately (Q1 FY27: 2). No segment-level PAT is disclosed anywhere in these pages.

years.source: Annual Report 2024 — page 108 (standalone, note 2.36); identical figures in consolidated note 2.44, page 154
Annual Report 2025 — page 110 (standalone, note 2.37); identical figures in consolidated note 2.45, page 158
Annual Report 2026 — page 112 (standalone, note 2.37); identical figures in consolidated note 2.45, page 161

latest_quarter.source: Presentation Aug 2026 — page 9 (Seamless EBITDA ₹151 cr; ERW ₹2 cr shown separately); page 10 EBIDTA mix confirms 151

verdict.not_found: No standalone financials for MSL Seamless Tubes Ltd / the demerged undertakings; no segment PAT; no segment-level quarterly revenue (only company-wide ₹1,266 cr for Q1 FY27); no demerger scheme pages.

verdict.rationale: This is not a spin-off of a business away from Sunteck Realty Ltd. (SRL) — it is an internal reorganisation that pulls a business up into the listed parent. On 1 October 2026 the board approved a Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013 between Satguru Corporate Services Private Limited (the Demerged Company, a wholly owned subsidiary of Sunteck) and Sunteck Realty Limited (the Resulting Company), demerging Satguru's 'Sunteck City 4th Avenue Undertaking' — the residential real estate project at ODC, Goregaon West — into Sunteck on a going-concern basis. The business being separated out of Satguru is large: its turnover for the year ended 31 March 2026 was approximately Rs 869 crore, about 77% of Sunteck's total consolidated turnover for FY26. That concentration is explained by the calls and accounts: Sunteck follows the project completion method, not percentage completion (Jan 2024 call), 4th Avenue received its occupation certificate and 'came up for revenue recognition' in FY26 (May 2025 call), and the Q3 FY26 revenue jump was attributed by CFO Prashant Chaubey directly to the completed 4th Avenue project (Feb 2026 call). The consequence visible in the Q1 FY27 filing is a hollow parent: FY26 standalone revenue from operations was only Rs 209.41 crore with a standalone loss after tax of Rs 19.67 crore, against consolidated revenue of Rs 1,123.84 crore and consolidated PAT of Rs 202.07 crore — i.e. the group's largest profit pool sat one level down in Satguru. The three stated benefits are purely structural: (1) consolidation of the Demerged Business Undertaking, (2) administrative and operational efficiencies, and (3) efficient pooling and deployment of financial and managerial resources, facilitating project-specific capital allocation and funding strategies — which echoes management's FY26 funding narrative of simultaneous capital needs at Nepeansea Road, Dubai and the 5th Avenue commercial build (Oct 2025 call, when Rs 500 crore of warrants were placed). No external party is named as having asked for it: the filings cite no investor, lender or JV-partner demand, no consideration, no share exchange ratio (Satguru is 100%-owned, so no shares are issued), no change in either shareholding pattern and no new listing; the Scheme is subject to statutory/regulatory approvals including the NCLT.
verdict.evolution: The idea never surfaced on any earnings call in the 36-month window: across Jan 2024, Jun 2024, Aug 2024, Nov 2024, Jan 2025, May 2025, Jul 2025, Oct 2025, Feb 2026, Apr 2026 and the Jul 22, 2026 Q1 FY27 call, neither the demerger, nor Satguru, nor any scheme of arrangement is mentioned — on 22 July 2026 Kamal Khetan instead said the Rs 2,250 crore fundraising resolution was 'obviously, enabling' with 'absolutely no planning of any fundraising'. What the calls did build was the predicate: the project completion method was reiterated in Jan 2024, 4th Avenue's occupation certificate and FY26 revenue recognition were flagged in May 2025, the Rs 500 crore preferential issue for Nepeansea/Dubai/5th Avenue funding came in Oct 2025, and the completed 4th Avenue was named as the FY26 revenue driver in Feb 2026 and Apr 2026 (FY26 operating revenue Rs 1,124 crore). Alongside, filings in Mar 2026 (Magenta Buildcon, Sunteck Infracon) and Apr 2026 (Mantavya Real Estates) show continuous subsidiary-level reshuffling into step-down holdings. The plan appears fully formed only at the 1 Oct 2026 board meeting (6.45-7.05 p.m.), where the Scheme was approved together with the appointment of EY as internal auditor to 31 March 2027.

points.point: The business separated is Satguru's residential project undertaking at ODC Goregaon West, demerged into listed parent Sunteck on a going-concern basis — an internal reorganisation, not a market spin-off.
points.quote: The Demerged Business Undertaking of the Demerged Company comprises of the residential real estate project under “Sunteck City 4th Avenue Undertaking” (as defined in the Scheme).

points.point: Size of what moves: ~Rs 869 crore of turnover for FY26, roughly 77% of Sunteck's entire consolidated turnover — the group's dominant revenue block sat inside the subsidiary.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Business Undertaking of Satguru for the year ended 31 March 2026 was Rs. ~869 Crs representing ~77% of the total consolidated turnover of Sunteck for the year ended 31st March 2026.

points.point: The stated problems solved are structural, not commercial: consolidation, administrative and operational efficiency, and the ability to allocate and fund capital project by project.
points.quote: Efficient pooling and deployment of financial resources, managerial resources and facilitate project-specific capital allocation and funding strategies.

points.point: No consideration, no share exchange ratio, no shareholding change and no new listing — confirming the purpose is balance-sheet and governance plumbing rather than value unlocking for shareholders.
points.quote: Since, Satguru is a wholly owned subsidiary of Sunteck, hence, no shares are proposed to be issued pursuant to the Scheme.

points.point: Execution risk is regulatory: the Scheme needs NCLT sanction, and the same 1 Oct 2026 board meeting also appointed EY as internal auditor to 31 March 2027.
points.quote: The Scheme is subject to the requisite statutory / regulatory approvals including the approval of National Company Law Tribunal.

points.point: Q1 FY27 filing shows the hollow-parent problem the demerger addresses: FY26 standalone revenue Rs 209.41 crore and a standalone loss of Rs 19.67 crore versus consolidated revenue Rs 1,123.84 crore; the parent also moved to the 115BAA tax regime in Q1 FY27.
points.quote: During the quarter ended 30 June 2026, the Company exercised the option to adopt the concessional tax regime under Section 115BAA of the Income-tax Act, 1961.

points.point: Pattern of ongoing intra-group reshuffling in the months before the Scheme: wholly owned subsidiaries pushed down into step-down holdings for Rs 1,00,000 each (Magenta/Sunteck Infracon in Mar 2026, Mantavya in Apr 2026).
points.quote: Pursuant to this Mantavya continues to be the subsidiary by way of Step down wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: CFO attributes the Q3 FY26 revenue jump squarely to the completed 4th Avenue project — the very undertaking later demerged out of Satguru.
points.quote: So Rishith, as you are aware, we have completed our Sunteck City 4th Avenue project in ODC Goregaon West. So the revenue jump that you see is coming from that project.

points.point: Management had pre-announced that 4th Avenue's occupation certificate would drive FY26 revenue recognition, which is why FY26 turnover concentrated in Satguru.
points.quote: With regards to revenue recognition definitely with the occupation certificate getting received for Sunteck City 4th Avenue so that project will come up for revenue recognition in FY26.

points.point: Project completion accounting explains the lumpy, entity-level concentration of revenue that the consolidation addresses.
points.quote: With respect to revenue recognition in the financial statement, I would like to reiterate today that per Ind AS, the Indian Accounting Standard, the company follows the project completion method and not the percentage completion method of accounting.

points.point: Context for 'project-specific capital allocation and funding': the Rs 500 crore preferential issue was raised against simultaneous funding needs at Nepeansea Road, Dubai and 5th Avenue commercial plus new BD.
points.quote: But at the same time, we were seeing that there will be a lot of requirement of the funds, which will be required in Nepeansea Road and Dubai, as well as commercial building of 5th Avenue, plus the new business development.

points.point: FY26 scale against which the Rs 869 crore demerged turnover should be read: consolidated operating revenue Rs 1,124 crore, EBITDA Rs 305 crore, PAT Rs 202 crore, net debt/equity 0.06x.
points.quote: On the full year basis, operating revenue stood at INR1,124 crores for FY '26.

points.point: Ten weeks before the board approved the Scheme, management disclosed nothing about restructuring and said the Rs 2,250 crore enabling resolution was routine with no fundraising planned.
points.quote: So, this is, obviously, enabling resolution. And if you see every year, we take this enabling resolution.

verdict.what_management_expects: Sunteck gains 4th Avenue's ~Rs 869 crore turnover — 77% of FY26 consolidated revenue — into standalone books that showed just ~Rs 209 crore revenue and a ~Rs 20 crore loss in FY26. Group-wide: administrative/operational efficiencies, pooled financial and managerial resources, project-specific capital allocation and funding. No margin, valuation or shareholding claims; no shares issued.
verdict.gaps: Calls never mention the demerger, Satguru, or any scheme; filings give no tax, debt, RERA, NCLT-timeline, appointed-date or accounting detail, no segment disclosure, and name no requesting stakeholder.

verdict.segment_name: Satguru Corporate Services Private Limited (the Demerged Business Undertaking — Sunteck City 4th Avenue); not reported as a separate segment
verdict.measure_notes: No segment-level P&L exists: both Sunteck Realty's standalone and consolidated segment notes (AR2024 p378, AR2025 p287/p392, AR2026 p133/p175) state the business is a single reportable segment ('Real Estate / Construction and Development of Real Estate projects and allied activities'), so no revenue/result is disclosed for the demerged undertaking as a segment. The only own-entity figures available are from the FY2026 Form AOC-I subsidiary table: 'Turnover (including other income)' — i.e. entity-level total income, not external segment revenue and not net of inter-company transactions; the profit line taken as operating_profit is 'Profit/(Loss) before Tax' (PBT, not segment result/EBIT/EBITDA), and pat is 'Profit/(Loss) after Tax'. These are standalone figures of the subsidiary legal entity (Satguru Corporate Services Pvt Ltd), which is not necessarily coterminous with the 4th Avenue undertaking being demerged.

Annual Report 2025 — page 287 / page 392 (single-segment note; no AOC-I or entity data on supplied pages)
Annual Report 2026 — page 176 (Form AOC-I, Part A: Subsidiaries, Sr. No. 2)

verdict.not_found: No segment/undertaking revenue, EBITDA or PAT for FY2024–FY2025; no quarterly or half-year figures for the demerged business — presentations report only consolidated Sunteck Realty results.

verdict.rationale: Management says the separation is a consolidation, not a divestment: a Composite Scheme of Arrangement approved 20 February 2026 that (1) merges UPL Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL SAS, the India crop protection business, 90.91% UPL-owned, FY25 turnover INR 24,120 Mn = 31.15% of UPL 1's turnover) into UPL Limited, (2) demerges that India Crop Protection Business into UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL 2), and (3) amalgamates UPL Crop Protection Holdings (UPL Cayman, 77.78% owned, FY25 turnover USD 4,187 Mn) into UPL 2 — leaving two listed companies: UPL Limited as a diversified agri-plus-specialty-chemicals platform (SUPERFORM stays with it as the manufacturing arm, and it keeps incubating new verticals) and UPL 2 as what the press release calls the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform across 140+ countries, with 9 R&D centres, 25 formulation facilities and a 14% innovation rate, led by Mike Frank. The problems they said it solves: a conglomerate/single-multiple valuation (Bikash Prasad: the market applies 'a single conglomerate multiple' and there is a 'huge conglomerate discount'), a complicated holding structure left over from the 2022 shareholder-approved simplification project that split India crop protection into UPL SAS while international crop protection sat under UPL Cayman, and private-market value not reaching the parent — Toshan Tamhane said that on the KKR and Alpha Wave valuations of Advanta 'the full value of that is not flowing through to UPL Limited.' They argue crop protection and seeds have fundamentally different cash-flow and capital-allocation needs, citing Corteva's own announced crop-protection/seeds split, and that independent capital and governance structures will let each platform raise capital separately, optimise its own capital structure and grow faster (Jai Shroff: 'at least 3x-4x the other players'). Deleveraging was the stated precondition and is now largely done — gross debt down from $3.8bn (FY24) to $2.3bn (FY26), net debt $3.1bn to $1.6bn, gearing 4.6x to below 1.6x — with Jai Shroff saying leverage 'was an issue which kept the multiple of the company' and 'is gone away now.' Who asked: investors/analysts drove it (the whole agenda came from investor feedback on the four below-EBITDA line items, debt and liquidity), KKR and Alpha Wave as platform-level investors wanted liquidity, and the Upswing Trust (an existing UPL SAS investor) swaps into UPL Cayman and ends up with 16.78% of UPL 2 as a public shareholder with one board nomination right; promoters locked their UPL 2 holding for 18 months from listing. Consideration is all-share: 1,000 UPL 1 shares per 48 UPL SAS shares; 1 UPL 2 share per 1 UPL 1 share on demerger; 1,000 UPL 2 shares per 213 UPL Cayman shares — no cash.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced as monetisation rather than separation: on the Jan 2025 call management announced Alpha Wave's $350m into Advanta ($100m primary, $250m secondary from UPL Ltd for ~12.44%) plus the $200m rights issue, all framed around getting net debt/EBITDA to ~2x. By Aug 2025 (Q1 FY26) it had become an open-ended structural review — Bikash Prasad said advisors were being engaged 'to explore unlocking value across all platforms' with no firm structure and no timeline, alongside a promise to 'significantly deleverage' over one to two years; Nov 2025 (Q2 FY26) repeated the same formula (restructuring, strategic fundraising, potential IPO) and added the DECCO post-harvest integration into Advanta, with Bikash hinting a corporate action would help fund the ~$900m FY27 maturities. Feb 2026 (Q3 FY26) was the first concrete step — Advanta's DRHP filed 19 January 2026 as a pure offer-for-sale (KKR 2.2%, UPL Ltd 7.8%) with proceeds 'largely for deleveraging', justified by the crop-protection-versus-seeds capital-allocation argument and the Corteva precedent, plus a stated 1-to-3-year window for corporate actions across all platforms; the crop-protection scheme itself was then approved on 20 February 2026 and, by the May 2026 Capital Markets Day, had drawn open shareholder opposition (Old Bridge's Tarang Agarwal warning of a HoldCo discount), with Bikash saying ten structures had been examined and that two months of unfiltered investor feedback would go to the board 'in a month or two'. Execution continued regardless: CCI approval 2/3 June 2026, BSE and NSE observation letters 29 July 2026, and the Swap and ESOP Swap Transactions completed 31 July 2026, with the Scheme still pending shareholder, creditor and NCLT approval as of the 2 November 2026 results.

points.point: The core move is consolidating the India crop protection business (UPL SAS) and the global crop protection business (UPL Cayman) into one entity, UPL 2, with its own manufacturing base, R&D, registrations and independent management.
points.quote: The Scheme proposes to consolidate the India Crop Protection Business held in UPL SAS and Global Crop Protection Business held in UPL Cayman, under a single entity, creating a focused, pure-play crop protection platform.

points.point: Two listed entities are meant to let investors choose their exposure — UPL 1 as diversified agri/specialty chemicals plus incubation, UPL 2 as dedicated crop protection.
points.quote: This will enable clearer value discovery by providing flexibility to the investors to select investments which best suit their investment strategies and risk profile.

points.point: Independent capital raising and capital-structure optimisation for each entity is given as a core benefit, alongside cost efficiencies from consolidated manufacturing and market access.
points.quote: The Scheme will allow UPL 1 and UPL 2 to raise capital independently, allowing each entity to optimize its capital structure and pursue business opportunities more efficiently and effectively.

points.point: The press release positions UPL 2 by scale — world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform, 140+ countries — as the route to faster innovation delivery and market share.
points.quote: Bringing our crop protection businesses under one platform creates the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform.

points.point: Bikash Prasad named the valuation problem directly: the market prices UPL on one conglomerate multiple, and separation is meant to make the sum of the parts visible.
points.quote: You know that even today market is valuing us using a single conglomerate multiple, they are applying on us.

points.point: He said the chosen structure was picked after reviewing roughly ten alternatives with advisors, and that independent capital and governance structures per platform will accelerate growth.
points.quote: So once these platforms have their independent capital structure, independent governance structure, it will grow much faster.

points.point: Jai Shroff framed it as brand-led, IP-rich, high-growth businesses needing autonomy, with SUPERFORM staying inside UPL Limited as the manufacturing platform.
points.quote: All these businesses need long-term need a kind of independent life, right?

points.point: He tied the timing to deleveraging being complete — leverage had suppressed the multiple and is no longer the constraint, so the re-rating can now come from structure.
points.quote: We've also made sure that the as in the past leverage was an issue for which kept the multiple of the company.

points.point: Old Bridge's Tarang Agarwal pushed back on the announced structure as value-destructive for existing UPL shareholders and urged alternative structures; Bikash said investor feedback would go unfiltered to the board.
points.quote: But the challenge is that the manner in which that the current structure has been announced, it's likely to trigger a significant HoldCo discount .

points.point: Toshan Tamhane gave the separation logic for seeds versus crop protection — different cash flows and capital allocation — explicitly citing Corteva's own split, and calling Advanta the eighth largest global seeds player.
points.quote: And lastly, third, we believe that the needs of crop protection in terms of the cash flows, capital allocation are very different from that of the seeds business.

points.point: He also said private-market valuations of Advanta (KKR, then Alpha Wave) were not being reflected in UPL Limited's own price — the public-market unlock argument.
points.quote: Because , if you look at the valuation that KKR and subsequently Alpha Wave came in at , at least we feel that the full value of that is no t flowing through to UPL Limited.

points.point: The Advanta DRHP (filed 19 January 2026) was a pure offer for sale — KKR 2.2%, UPL Limited 7.8% — with no money going into Advanta and proceeds earmarked for group deleveraging.
points.quote: But it will come to the group largely for deleveraging of the group balance sheet.

verdict.rationale: SKF India separated its Industrial bearings business out of the listed company into SKF India (Industrial) Limited, leaving SKF India Ltd as a pure-play Automotive bearings company (management called it a "reverse carve-out" mirroring SKF AB's global split of Automotive, ~30% of group revenue versus 34-35% in India). Management's stated logic rested on three pillars: fundamentally different macro drivers (Automotive: EV/CAFE and BS-VII emission norms, 30% EV penetration target by 2030, premiumization/SUVs, last-mile commercial vehicles; Industrial: infrastructure spend, Make in India/NIP/PLI, China-Plus-One, railways/metro/Vande Bharat, wind and renewables doubling by 2030); different customer needs (a few large auto OEMs needing application-specific, longer-cycle engineered products — 60-65% engineered order in Auto versus ~25-30% in Industrial — against hundreds of industrial verticals wanting uptime, condition monitoring and remanufacturing); and a different manufacturing philosophy (Auto = large batch, small/medium bearings, automation and cycle-time efficiency; Industrial = wide assortment, small/large sizes, flexible lines with fast changeover plus a large traded component). The problems they said this solves: management attention split across two unlike businesses, capital allocation that could not be tailored (Auto was short of capacity, Industrial needed a brand-new Pune plant and localization from ~30-35% toward 70%), slow decision-making and launches, mismatched innovation cycles, and poor financial visibility for investors in a combined P&L. Operationally the split was defined down to the line: Bangalore 10 lines (7 Auto, 3 Industrial, with those 3 moving to Pune so Bangalore becomes 100% Auto), Pune 22 lines (12 Auto, 10 Industrial), Haridwar 4 lines all Auto; land 85:15 in Bangalore, 52:48 in Pune, 100% Auto in Haridwar; manpower 55-60% Auto versus 40-45% Industrial; cash allocated on the two businesses' last three years of profits. Shareholders received one SKF Industrial share of Rs 10 for every SKF India share held (PwC Business Consulting share entitlement report dated 24 December 2024; Saffron Capital fairness opinion 25 December 2024), with pre-demerger cost of acquisition apportioned 46.88% to SKF India and 53.12% to SKF Industrial. Pro forma FY24 economics shown to investors were Auto ~18% EBITDA and Industrial ~17%, both ~16% PBT, off a combined FY24 revenue of INR 45.7 billion; FY25 combined revenue was INR 4,919.9 crore (+7.65%) with PBT INR 763.1 crore (+3.71%). Nobody external demanded the separation — it was a group-level decision, with investors on the calls supportive (one explicitly "wholeheartedly supported" it) while pressing for structural clarity given SKF would still have three Indian entities including the unlisted SKF Engineering & Lubrication (Ahmedabad plant, global technical centre, lubrication and sealing factories); no lender or partner requirement was ever cited.
verdict.evolution: The demerger was announced in Q4 CY2024 and first explained in detail on a dedicated update call on 9 April 2025, which laid out the three macro/customer/manufacturing drivers, the six enablers (management focus, manufacturing efficiency, tailored capital, agility, innovation, investor visibility), pro forma FY24 carve-out financials and a 12-15 month timeline, plus an aspiration of "2 to 3 more points" of EBITDA. By the 19 May 2025 Q4 call the plant allocation had firmed up (Haridwar 100% Auto, Bangalore ~80-85% Auto, a new Industrial factory beside the Pune plant), and the 30 June 2025 investor meet added line-by-line, land and manpower splits, segment revenue mixes from FY22-FY25, three-year guidance (Auto 10-12%, Industrial 8-10% to FY28, margins held at 17-19%) and a step-up in capex from ~INR 150 crore to roughly INR 350-400 crore a year (INR 450-500 crore Pune industrial plant by 2028, INR 500-600 crore Auto capex to 2030); the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting on 14 July 2025 approved the 1:1 scheme, and the 6-7 August 2025 AGM and Q1 FY26 call quantified the cost for the first time (INR 184 million in Q1, mostly SAP/IT separation and consultants, 1.5-2% margin drag running into H1 FY27, plus stamp duty on asset transfer) while conceding the businesses were "so deeply integrated" that separation was complex. After NCLT sanction on 26 September 2025, effectiveness on 1 October 2025 and a 15 October 2025 record date, the story changed tone: the 21 May 2026 call presented SKF India as a standalone automotive company guiding to only 11-12% PBT margin (FY26 EBITDA 15.3%) with investors complaining that disclosure had "dropped substantially" post-demerger and that margins were far below what was promised in the run-up to the demerger vote, management answering that royalty was unchanged and this was a transition.

points.point: The stated purpose: two independent, fit-for-purpose companies that each accelerate growth and profitability, driven by three differences — industry dynamics, customer needs and manufacturing philosophy.
points.quote: The intention of this demerger is to create 2 fit-for-purposes independent companies, which will accelerate both growth and profitability of both companies.

points.point: Management summarised the rationale as three separate axes of difference, with manufacturing efficiency and customer service as the payoff.
points.quote: So to summarize, macro drivers are different. Customer drivers and innovation is different; and third, the manufacturing itself, the process of manufacturing itself is very different, what will make us most efficient and help us serve the customer needs.

points.point: Manufacturing philosophy was the concrete operating problem: Auto runs large batches of small/medium bearings for few OEMs with automation and economies of scale, while Industrial needs flexible lines, customised solutions and a large traded/regional component.
points.quote: Automotive has a large batch sizes with small and medium-sized bearings.

points.point: Margin ambition attached to the separation: 2-3 percentage points of EBITDA upside in both businesses, from more efficient manufacturing, procurement and value-based pricing of premium products such as ceramic and energy-efficient bearings.
points.quote: So I would say while the margins are typically relatively thin, we would hope that we can get at least 2 to 3 more points on our EBITDA going forward.

points.point: Shareholders were told the split was economically neutral — a mirror shareholding with a 1:1 share issue and listing of SKF Industrial on both exchanges.
points.quote: The new company will mirror the shareholding of the existing listed company with each shareholder of SKF India receiving one share of SKF Industrial as a consideration of the demerger.

points.point: Investor visibility into the two businesses' separate performance was explicitly listed as one of the demerger benefits, alongside tailored capital deployment and two different manufacturing philosophies.
points.quote: and finally, just more visibility for the -- our investors, all of you, to be able to see the performance of the 2 entities independently.

points.point: Pro forma FY24 carve-out economics given to investors: Automotive ~18% EBITDA, Industrial ~17%, both around 16% PBT, with capex set to double from INR 130-150 crore as a new Industrial plant is built next to the existing Pune site.
points.quote: So if you look at FY '24, our EBITDA margins for automotive was around 18%. And industrial was around 17%.

points.point: The asset split was disclosed line by line — Bangalore 10 lines 70:30 with three lines moving to Pune so Bangalore becomes 100% Automotive, Pune 52:48 land, Haridwar 100% Automotive, manpower roughly 55:45.
points.quote: There are three main plants, as we said, Bangalore, Pune and Haridwar. Bangalore, today there are 10 lines that will be split in the ratio of 70 to 30.

points.point: Three-year guidance for the two entities: Automotive 10-12% growth, Industrial 8-10% (held back until the new Pune plant and localization land in FY27-28), with margins maintained at 17-19% and upside beyond FY28.
points.quote: Next 3 years till '28, we expect growth in automotive to be in the 10 % to 12% range, industrial to be a little lower, 8% to 10% range.

points.point: Capital allocation was the hard constraint being fixed: a brand-new Industrial-only Pune plant (DGBB, TRB, unitised bearings) costing INR 450-500 crore by 2028 plus INR 350-450 crore of additional lines, on top of INR 500-600 crore of Automotive capex to 2030.
points.quote: Pune, we will be setting up a new plant, fully industrial, for industrial, making primarily DGBBs, which are deep groove ball bearings, tapered roller bearings, and unitized bearings, which are UCs.

points.point: At the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting, management conceded the separation was complex precisely because the two businesses were deeply intertwined, and said the total demerger cost was still being accumulated.
points.quote: As you know, it's a complex project primarily because the businesses both automotive and industrial, they are so deeply integrated that having two independent businesses is a complex process.

points.point: An existing institutional shareholder (Ravi Purohit) publicly backed the demerger while asking why India would still be left with three SKF entities when the group was simplifying structures; management said no merger of entities was contemplated until the demerger completed.
points.quote: And first of all, we'd like to congratulate and have wholeheartedly supported this demerger initiative that SKF Group is undertaking.

points.point: First quantification of the cost: INR 184 million in Q1 FY26, mainly SAP and separate data infrastructure plus compliance consultants, with a 1.5-2% margin drag expected to run to H1 FY27 and extra stamp duty/registration cost on asset transfer in the Industrial entity.
points.quote: So if you look at our current quarter, cost of demerger was around INR184 million.

points.point: At the FY25 AGM the Chairman framed the demerger as strategic repositioning to sharpen focus, improve execution agility and deepen customer alignment, with manufacturing roadmaps diverging (Automotive automation-led high throughput; Industrial modular and demand-responsive).
points.quote: The announcement of our demerger, which is separating the automotive and industrial businesses into two focused publicly listed entities was a significant milestone.

points.point: Post-demerger, management clarified the direction of the carve-out — Industrial was hived off and the listed SKF India Limited is the automotive division, a reverse of the group-level split.
points.quote: But in India, it is a reverse carve -out where industrial has gone out. So SKF India Limited remains as automotive division.

points.point: The promised margin uplift did not appear: FY26 PBT fell 694 bps, EBITDA was 15.3%, and guidance was reset to 11-12% PBT, with Auto still buying medium DGBB and tapered roller bearings from SKF Industrial because of its own capacity shortage.
points.quote: Now talking about the sustainable margin, we could be looking at 11 -12% kind of margin in the near future, while obviously in long term, the focus would be on improving it further, but the sustainable margin will be that.

points.point: A long-term shareholder attacked the post-demerger communication gap, noting pre-demerger guidance of 16-19% (even 18-19%) EBITDA for a 95%-localised Auto business and a 50-70% valuation discount to Schaeffler and Timken; management replied royalty was unchanged and there is now no pure-play comparable.
points.quote: Increasingly, our post demerger, what we are realizing is that the investor communication and the disclosures have dropped substantially.

points.point: Management's closing framing still rested on focus and agility as the value-unlock, with restructuring costs described as a temporary hit.
points.quote: The demerger positions us to unlock greater value by enabling sharper focus and agility in our business.

points.point: The scheme transferred the Industrial business as a going concern into SKF India (Industrial) Limited under Sections 230-232, effective 1 October 2025 (NCLT order 26 September 2025, record date 15 October 2025), with pre-demerger cost of acquisition apportioned 46.88% to SKF India and 53.12% to SKF Industrial — i.e. Industrial was the larger half.
points.quote: The Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench, vide its Order dated 26th September, 2025, sanctioned the Scheme of Arrangement between SKF India Limited ("the Company" or "Demerged Company") and SKF India (Industrial) Limited ("SKF Industrial" or "Resulting Company") and their respective shareholders and creditors under Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 ("Scheme"), providing for the demerger of the Company's Industrial Business (Demerged Undertaking as defined in the Scheme ) into SKF Industrial on a going concern basis

points.point: The post-completion press release restated the purpose as two focused entities with independent boards and governance, and attached separate investment plans — Industrial INR 8,000-9,500 million by 2030 including a new Pune facility by 2028, Automotive INR 4,100-5,100 million by 2030 across EV, two-wheeler and wheel-end capacity in Haridwar, Pune and Bangalore.
points.quote: The demerger, sanctioned by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) and approved by shareholders earlier this year, has formally separated SKF India's business into two focused entities — SKF Industrial and SKF Automotive — each equipped with independent boards and governance structures.

points.point: The FY26 AGM presentation codified the five official reasons for the separation and rebranded the automotive entity as SKF Vertevo, reporting FY26 revenue of INR 21,295 million, 15% EBITDA margin and EPS of INR 23.7.
points.quote: Why the Demerger? Different Market Dynamics Distinct Customer Needs Focused Capital Allocation Faster Decision Making Independent Growth Strategies

verdict.what_management_expects: Two fit-for-purpose entities growing faster and more profitably: automotive 10-12% and industrial 8-10% growth to FY28, both holding 17-19% EBITDA with 2-3 points of upside later; sharper management focus, tailored capital deployment and manufacturing efficiency, plus separate financial visibility attracting more aligned investors.
verdict.gaps: Never quantified: total demerger cost, dis-synergies, inter-entity trading/rent/service charges, or why post-demerger margins (11-12% PBT) fall far below the 16-19% promised pre-demerger.

Revenue is the segment's total revenue (exports allocated into the two businesses), since Industrial + Automotive revenue sums exactly to company revenue (31,909 + 17,290 = 49,199.2 MINR FY2025; 28,979 + 16,722 = 45,701 MINR FY2024); segment EBITDA and PAT likewise sum to company EBITDA 8,469 and PAT 5,658 (FY2025) and PAT 5,517.7 (FY2024). verdict.rationale: The separation is a two-part composite Scheme of Arrangement and Amalgamation approved by the Thermax board on July 30, 2026 (Sections 230–232, Companies Act 2013; Appointed Date April 1, 2026; subject to NCLT Mumbai), involving two wholly owned subsidiaries: Thermax Bioenergy Solutions Private Limited (TBSPL) and Thermax Cooling Solutions Limited (TCSL). First, the Bio-CNG EPC undertaking of TBSPL — described as the 'Technology, Engineering, Procurement and Construction scope for Bio-Compressed Natural Gas (Bio CNG) projects', with FY26 turnover of Rs. 239.35 crore, i.e. 3.67% of the listed entity's standalone turnover — is demerged out of TBSPL and merged into Thermax Limited, while the Operations & Maintenance (O&M) business stays behind in TBSPL. The stated reason is that the EPC undertaking 'is in line with the business of the Company', so similar businesses are consolidated into the listed parent, leaving TBSPL's management free to 'focus on the remaining segment O&M'; the broader objective is to 're-organize and segregate the different business verticals and focus on core businesses', so that 'the two entities can each pursue growth opportunities that are more aligned with their own industry dynamics, leading to improved operational efficiencies and profitability'. Second, TCSL — a near-dormant entity (FY26 total income Rs. 0.8 crore, net worth Rs. 0.6 crore, paid-up capital Rs. 10.0 crore, doing energy projects, an Energy Exchange Platform, electrostatic precipitators and regenerative air preheaters) — is merged into Thermax Limited 'to simplify overall group structure and reduce administrative overheads', with management expecting 'a significant improvement in certain key financial ratios', 'annual cost savings for the Thermax Group' and metrics that 'convey stronger financial stability and valuation metrics'. The financial backdrop for the Bio-CNG leg is weak: TBSPL carried a negative net worth of Rs. (106.9) crore on FY26 total income of Rs. 260.9 crore, Thermax took a Rs. 30 crore impairment on its TBSPL investment in Q3 FY26, bio-CNG was repeatedly cited as a drag (low-margin legacy orders, orders 'not as per our expectations'), and in Q1 FY27 the group reclassified TBSPL out of Industrial Infra into Green Solutions. Mechanically it is a pure internal reorganisation: both entities are wholly owned, no shares or cash consideration pass, Thermax's shares in TCSL are cancelled, TBSPL remains an unlisted wholly owned subsidiary, there is no change in shareholding pattern or control, and the Scheme 'will have no impact on the consolidated financial statements / results of the Company'.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaces in the filings as a sequence of group-simplification steps rather than in any call: Thermax first took TBSPL from 65% to 76.97% via a rights issue (May 7, 2025) and then to 100% by buying Everenviro's 23.03% (completed August 20, 2025), making a clean demerger possible; on October 17, 2025 the board approved the merger of Buildtech Products India into Thermax on consolidation/compliance-reduction logic (NCLT sanction June 2, 2026, received June 3, 2026), and on February 4, 2026 two step-down wind subsidiaries (Jalansar into Kanakal) were amalgamated on the same consolidation, synergy and compliance-cost reasoning. Alongside, the Feb 2, 2026 Q3 FY26 release and the May 8, 2026 Q4 FY26 call flagged bio-CNG as the weak spot — low-margin legacy orders being worked off, orders 'not as per our expectations', projects in performance-trial stage — and a Rs. 30 crore impairment was taken on the TBSPL investment in Q3 FY26. The composite Scheme itself was only approved and disclosed on July 30, 2026, with Appointed Date April 1, 2026, in the same board meeting as Q1 FY27 results; the Q1 FY27 filing also recorded the segment realignment of TBSPL from Industrial Infra to Green Solutions, so by then the plan had become 'EPC into the listed parent, O&M left in TBSPL' plus the absorption of TCSL. No earnings call in the readable record discusses the Scheme, because the only call with extractable text (May 2026) predates the July 30, 2026 board approval.

points.point: The board approved a composite scheme on July 30, 2026 demerging TBSPL's Bio-CNG EPC undertaking into Thermax Limited while O&M stays in TBSPL, and merging Thermax Cooling Solutions Limited into Thermax Limited; Appointed Date April 1, 2026, subject to NCLT.
points.quote: The Scheme of Arrangement and Amalgamation provides for demerger of EPC business undertaking of the Demerged Company which is involved in business of Technology, Engineering, Procurement and Construction scope for Bio-Compressed Natural Gas (Bio CNG) projects.

points.point: Rationale for pulling EPC out of TBSPL: the EPC work duplicates the parent's own business, so similar businesses are consolidated into the listed entity.
points.quote: The demerged undertaking business is in line with the business of the Company and thus the management has decided to consolidate the similar businesses by demerging the EPC segment into the Company.

points.point: What the residual entity gets: TBSPL is left as a focused O&M services company for bio-CNG projects.
points.quote: The management of Demerged Company believes that the demerger of EPC will help them focus on the remaining segment O&M, wherein they can undertake various operation and maintenance services for projects.

points.point: The overarching objective is stated as segregating business verticals so each entity can chase opportunities matched to its own industry dynamics.
points.quote: In this manner, the two entities can each pursue growth opportunities that are more aligned with their own industry dynamics, leading to improved operational efficiencies and profitability.

points.point: The demerged Bio-CNG EPC undertaking is small relative to the parent: FY26 turnover Rs. 239.35 crore, 3.67% of the listed entity's turnover for the year ended March 31, 2026.
points.quote: The turnover of demerged undertaking as on March 31, 2026 was Rs. 239.35 Crores

points.point: The entity being carved up is balance-sheet impaired: TBSPL shows negative net worth of Rs. (106.9) crore against total income of Rs. 260.9 crore and paid-up capital of Rs. 38.0 crore, versus Thermax's net worth of Rs. 4,427.09 crore.
Rationale for absorbing Thermax Cooling Solutions Limited: group-structure simplification, lower administrative overheads, better key financial ratios and annual cost savings.
points.quote: In order to simplify overall group structure and reduce administrative overheads, Management has proposed consolidation of Transferor Company with the Company which is expected to result in a significant improvement in certain key financial ratios.

points.point: An explicitly presentational/valuation motive is given for the TCSL merger — consolidating resources is expected to signal stronger financial stability and valuation metrics.
points.quote: Such consolidation of resources is also anticipated to convey stronger financial stability and valuation metrics, thereby presenting a more accurate picture of the Company's financial strength and long-term prospects.

points.point: It is an all-internal reshuffle: both subsidiaries are wholly owned, no consideration or shares are issued, Thermax's TCSL shares are cancelled, and TBSPL stays an unlisted wholly owned subsidiary.
points.quote: There will be no change in the shareholding pattern of the Company pursuant to the Scheme, as no shares are being issued by the Transferee Company in connection with the Scheme.

points.point: No consolidated earnings or control effect is claimed; the mergers are common-control business combinations under Appendix C to Ind AS 103.
points.quote: The Scheme will have no impact on the consolidated financial statements / results of the Company and will not result in any change in the Company's shareholding pattern or control structure.

points.point: TBSPL was first taken to 100% ownership (65% to 76.97% via the May 7, 2025 rights issue, then the balance 23.03% bought from Everenviro, effective August 20, 2025), which is what makes a no-consideration demerger possible.
points.quote: Pursuant to the completion of this transaction , TBSPL has become a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company effective August 20, 2025.

points.point: The parent had already written down its TBSPL exposure: a Rs. 30 crore impairment charge on the investment in Thermax Bioenergy Solutions was booked as an exceptional item in Q3 FY26 (part of standalone exceptional items of Rs. 85.38 crore).
points.quote: b. Thermax Bioenergy Solutions Private Limited* (30 00)

points.point: Just before the Scheme, TBSPL was moved out of Industrial Infra into the Green Solutions segment as part of an organizational restructuring aligned with business strategy, with all prior periods restated.
points.quote: During the current quarter, the Group reassessed its segment reporting under Ind AS 108 -Operating Segments following an organizational restructuring aligned with its business strategy.

points.point: The same simplification logic had already been applied in the Buildtech Products India merger (board October 17, 2025; NCLT order June 2, 2026) — fewer duplicate compliances, lower overheads, pooled cash flows.
points.quote: The merger will result in a reduction in the multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances required at present to be separately carried out by the Transferor Company and the Transferee Company.

points.point: And in the February 4, 2026 amalgamation of step-down wind subsidiaries Jalansar into Kanakal, with the same stated benefits of consolidation, synergy and compliance/administrative cost savings.
points.quote: Cost savings in terms of administrative, managerial, and compliance expenses.

points.point: On the Q4 FY26 call, management said the low-margin legacy orders sat specifically in bio-CNG (plus FGD and Projects & Energy Solutions) and were almost fully executed, with bio-CNG jobs in performance trials to be closed in Q1-Q2 FY27.
points.quote: On those low-margin orders that we had specifically in our bio-CNG business as well as our FGD business , as well as some bit on our Projects and Energy Solutions business. I think we almost executed them.

points.point: Management flagged bio-CNG order inflow as a structural disappointment inside Industrial Infra, attributing it to a change in the market, while saying it still expects a better market later.
points.quote: But otherwise, I think it's been there's been a change in the market , and I think there's some bit of slowdown and Bio-CNG business order book has also been not as per our expectations.

points.point: Management nonetheless framed bio-CNG as a forward opportunity helped by state-government policy support, i.e. a business worth keeping rather than exiting.
points.quote: But just to mention and simultaneously in another one, Bio-CNG -- where we see more of state government policies coming in to support that, is in a similar way , a better opportunity that is going to come in for our Bio-CNG business.

points.point: Context on EPC project risk being absorbed into the parent: the same July 30, 2026 board meeting reported a Rs. 91 crore cost overrun on one Industrial Infra project, which cut Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT to Rs. 22 crore from Rs. 151 crore.
points.quote: The current quarter's results were impacted by a Rs. 91 crore increase in the estimated cost to complete one specific project in the Industrial Infra segment, arising from events identified during the quarter.

verdict.what_management_expects: For Thermax Limited: consolidation of similar EPC work in-house, simplified group structure, lower administrative overheads, annual group cost savings, significantly improved key financial ratios, and stronger perceived financial stability and valuation metrics. For TBSPL: a focused Bio-CNG O&M services company. For both: growth aligned to each one's industry dynamics, improved operational efficiency and profitability. No consolidated financial impact; no shareholding or control change.
verdict.gaps: No earnings call in the readable record discusses the Scheme (10 of 11 transcripts unextractable). No quantified cost savings, ratio targets, margin or valuation impact; no named investor, lender or partner request; no reason for keeping O&M separate.

verdict.segment_name: Thermax Bioenergy Solutions Private Limited (TBSPL) — the Bio-CNG EPC business being separated; no separate 'EPC business undertaking' segment is reported (Bio CNG sits inside the Industrial Infra segment)

Revenue line is 'Total income' (includes other income; not an external-vs-inter-segment split). Profit line available is (loss)/profit before tax and (loss)/profit for the period (PAT); no EBIT/EBITDA or operating-profit line is given, so operating_profit is left null — depreciation and finance costs are disclosed separately but an operating profit is not stated.
