DR Axion India Limited (formerly DR Axion India Private Limited) (Amalgamating Company 3)
verdict.reason: Aluminium business and expansion land are fragmented across entities; consolidation under a single focused operating entity gives a stronger balance sheet, unified asset ownership, simplified structure, better managerial focus and efficiency
verdict.insiders: Promoter/CMD Srinivasan Ravi sold 5,25,000 shares (2.01%) on 23 June 2026, holding falling 40.15% to 38.14%; no promoter shares issued in the merged subsidiary
verdict.hidden_value: Aluminium is now the largest segment (H1 FY27 revenue Rs 3,29,879 lakhs) but lowest-margin; DR Axion turnover Rs 1,298.52 cr on net worth Rs 511.34 cr versus Sunbeam Rs 1,237.46 cr on Rs 107.43 cr; consolidated borrowings Rs 3,61,860 lakhs
verdict.selling_pressure_why: No shares distributed to listed shareholders; Company not a party and its shareholding pattern is unaffected
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated — on 11 March 2026 the Company said "Not applicable. The Company is not a party to the proposed Scheme, and the shareholding pattern of the Company will not be affected by the proposed Scheme."
verdict.read_next: Draft Composite Scheme filed with NCLT, plus Aluminium Products segment EBIT margin in the next quarterly results
verdict.quote: This opportunity can be better capitalized by consolidating the Aluminium business under a single focused operating entity having a stronger balance sheet, a broader product and manufacturing base, unified asset ownership, and a streamlined organizational structure.

verdict.rationale: The separation is the carve-out and consolidation of the aluminium products business — Craftsman's own high-pressure die-casting aluminium division plus wholly owned subsidiaries DR Axion India and Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions — into one wholly owned aluminium operating entity, approved for evaluation by the Board on 13 February 2026 and begun as a phased composite scheme on 11 March 2026 (step-down subsidiaries Suprash Developers and Srikara Technologies into DR Axion, then DR Axion into Sunbeam, with Sunbeam's equity reorganised to Re 1 face value and 1 Sunbeam share at Rs 9 premium issued per DR Axion share of Rs 10). Management's core stated problem is subscale fragmentation: Ravi said global aluminium competitors run $3–6 billion (top ten $3–8 billion, one peer $8 billion in aluminium alone) while Craftsman is 'less than $0.5 billion in aluminium revenue', so going to the same customers as three separate businesses of $100m, $200m and $300m to win a single $100–200m order is 'becoming unwieldy… very expensive'. The three units overlap operationally — 'some equipment, some people, some processes may be redundant' — and marketing 'these small subsegments' separately is hard, so the fix is one vendor code and one customer face: 'with one vendor code or with the same customer base, we can operate the capacities.' Capacity reallocation is the second driver: Sunbeam's utilisation is being cut from ~70% to 45–50% as it exits ~10 minuscule customers (5% of revenue), legacy 10–15-year-old products and a piston line of ~INR30 crore revenue sold to Shriram Pistons for Rs 28 crore, while DR Axion is full at 80–85% and must expand, and Craftsman has no Chennai aluminium plant — 'When we going to put a plant there for the DR Axion, then again, one more plant for Craftsman doesn't make sense.' The scheme filing adds that the aluminium business and the land needed for expansion sat in different entities, 'resulting in the fragmentation of operations and asset ownership' — the ~50 acres at Sriperumbudur bought for about INR150 crore via Suprash and Srikara is leased to DR Axion — so merging aligns land, infrastructure and operations in one entity with a stronger balance sheet, broader manufacturing base and streamlined structure. Management frames all of it as the first leg toward a $1 billion aluminium business in 2–3 years, against an aluminium base it approximated at INR6,500 crore in FY2027. Asked directly whether consolidation was a deleveraging route (Karthi, Suyash Advisors), Ravi said no — 'It will be more to fund our future investments maybe' — pointing instead to net debt/EBITDA of 2.43 falling below 2 and then 1.5 naturally.
verdict.evolution: The idea began as post-acquisition synergy talk: on the Oct 2024 call (24 Oct 2024) Ravi said the plan was to 'commonize the business development strategy' across Craftsman, DR Axion and Sunbeam given their non-overlapping customers and complementary casting processes, and by the Nov 2025 call (10 Nov 2025) he described shared resources reducing 'the overhead burden on each of the companies'. On the Feb 2026 call (29 Jan 2026) the teams had been 'more or less integrated… on the working side' and exhibited jointly at EUROGUSS, and he closed by saying there were 'more interesting things to do… to make the company more strategically aligned' — two weeks later, on 13 February 2026, the Board approved evaluating consolidation of the aluminium business at a single wholly owned subsidiary level, and on 11 March 2026 decided it must be done 'in a phased manner', approving only Phase 1 (step-downs into DR Axion, DR Axion into Sunbeam). By the May 2026 call (8 May 2026) Ravi confirmed the scope had widened beyond the subsidiaries to Craftsman's own aluminium division — 'The easy one was how to do it with the DR and Sunbeam. It's also related to Craftsman aluminium business' — and the 28 October 2026 results still carry the scheme as pending NCLT approval.

points.point: Ravi confirmed the restructuring covers not just the two subsidiaries but Craftsman's own aluminium division, with the subsidiary merger treated as the easy first step.
points.quote: We look at our public disclosure, we also mentioned that not only Sunbeam and DR, we also looked at our aluminium business of Craftsman also.

points.point: The central rationale is scale versus $3–6 billion global competitors: bidding $100–200 million orders as three separate $100m–$300m businesses is unwieldy and expensive.
points.quote: When we go with each of the businesses at $200 million, $100 million revenue or $300 million revenue and try to take an order for $100 million, $200 million, it is to share the resources and to grow the business, it is becoming unwieldy.

points.point: He named duplicated equipment, people and processes and the difficulty of marketing small subsegments separately as the operational problem being solved.
points.quote: What I'm trying to say is that some equipment, some people, some processes may be redundant here. We may have customer base. It's difficult to do marketing with these small subsegments in the business.

points.point: Capacity reallocation is an explicit purpose: Sunbeam's utilisation drops from ~70% to 45–50% as it exits unviable legacy products and customers, and that capacity moves to the group's new customers under one vendor code.
points.quote: That is one of the reasons for our restructuring, if you have seen, so that we can, with one vendor code or with the same customer base, we can operate the capacities.

points.point: Plant economics drive it too — Craftsman has no Chennai aluminium plant, DR Axion's plant is full at 80–85% and needs a new campus, and building two separate plants there makes no sense.
points.quote: We want to create a separate campus for that and add aluminium business of Craftsman, which is high pressure die casting mainly. Then DR's plant is full, we have to expand DR Axion. When we going to put a plant there for the DR Axion, then again, one more plant for Craftsman doesn't make sense.

points.point: The merger is tied to the stated $1 billion aluminium ambition, with the aluminium business approximated at around INR6,500 crore in FY2027 (explicitly not guidance).
points.quote: Our stated ambition on the aluminium business, in the last year, I think I had mentioned a couple of times at least during the earnings call, that the first leg or first phase will be to touch $1 billion on the aluminium business. For that, we are also increasing the focus by merging the entities of the business model, which we have also put -up disclosures in the stock exchange.

points.point: Asked by Karthi (Suyash Advisors) whether consolidating aluminium was a deleveraging route against INR3,300 crore of debt, Ravi said it was about funding future investment, with net debt/EBITDA of 2.43 falling below 2 then to 1.5 anyway.
points.quote: It will be more to fund our future investments maybe, but I think this debt portion of it, debt to EBITDA- wise, if you look at it, the forward- looking EBITDA, I think we are already at 2.43 net debt to EBITDA.

points.point: The newly acquired land-holding vehicles Suprash Developers and Srikara Technologies (~50 acres near SIPCOT for about INR150 crore, for DR Axion's Sriperumbudur greenfield) are to be absorbed so no subsidiaries remain.
points.quote: All this will get merged when we are doing the scheme of things, whatever we have filed. There will be no subsidiary once that is. . .

points.point: Scale was already the argument before the Board acted: Craftsman is below $0.5 billion in aluminium against peers of $3–8 billion, and management said it cannot even bid for large orders without scaling.
points.quote: And you know that the stated fact is we are less than $0.5 billion in aluminium revenue. So unless we scale up capacity, we cannot even bid for the orders.

points.point: Operational integration of the three aluminium teams was already underway ahead of any legal merger, including a joint appearance at EUROGUSS Nuremberg, pending Sunbeam's full restructuring.
points.quote: While we wait for the total restructuring of Sunbeam to happen thoroughly, we have more or less integrated the three teams on the working side of it.

points.point: Closing the call, Ravi flagged a coming structural step without naming it — two weeks before the Board approved evaluating the aluminium consolidation on 13 February 2026.
points.quote: We have more interesting things to do in the -- to make the company more strategically aligned in line with the global requirements.

points.point: The synergy logic was framed in overhead and shared-resource terms, with Sunbeam expected to converge on group margin levels because resources are shared across the three aluminium businesses.
points.quote: In fact, acquiring Sunbeam is also helping Craftsman to acquire more customers and also to reduce the overhead burden on each of the companies.

points.point: Shared campuses were already producing the effect ahead of the scheme — Sunbeam's Gurgaon operations were moved into Craftsman's Bhiwadi site and run as one unit, averaging fixed costs.
points.quote: When we are having a campus, for example at Bhiwadi, it is not only we have shifted the Gurgaon facilities into Bhiwadi, Sunbeam's plant is operational as one unit inside the Craftsman Bhiwadi area.

points.point: At acquisition, the stated plan was to commonise go-to-market across the three complementary aluminium units (Craftsman high-pressure, DR Axion gravity/low-pressure, Sunbeam low-tonnage) — the seed of the later merger.
points.quote: And what we are first thinking is to commonize the business development strategy. That will be very important to tap the new opportunities across the globe.

points.point: Subscale against global peers was already the framing, with the group below $0.5 billion in aluminium versus competitors of $1.5–7 billion.
points.quote: I have always been saying that the -- our aluminum competition outside the world between $1.5 billion to $6 billion, $7 billion in revenue.

points.point: The 13 February 2026 Board filing defines the scope: consolidating Craftsman's own aluminium products business together with its aluminium subsidiaries into a single wholly owned subsidiary, by scheme of arrangement or other mode.
points.quote: This evaluation will cover the restructuring/consolidation of the aluminium products business of the Company, together with its wholly owned subsidiaries engaged in the aluminium product business, at a single wholly owned subsidiary level, as well as consolidation of other wholly owned subsidiaries, through such modes as may be considered appropriate, including but not limited to a scheme of arrangement under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013 and other applicable laws.

points.point: The 11 March 2026 scheme names the structural defect: operating business and the land/infrastructure needed to expand it sit in different entities.
points.quote: At present, the Aluminium business and the land and infrastructure required for its expansion are housed in different entities, resulting in the fragmentation of operations and asset ownership.

points.point: The stated benefit is one focused operating entity with a stronger balance sheet, broader product and manufacturing base, unified asset ownership and streamlined structure, to capture expected industry growth.
points.quote: This opportunity can be better capitalized by consolidating the Aluminium business under a single focused operating entity having a stronger balance sheet, a broader product and manufacturing base, unified asset ownership, and a streamlined organizational structure.

points.point: Absorbing the land-holding step-down subsidiaries into DR Axion is justified by the approved new aluminium facility on that leased land, to align land, infrastructure and operations in one entity.
points.quote: It is expected that consolidation of the Step-Down Subsidiaries with DRA will lead to efficient implementation of the approved expansion plans, seamless development of manufacturing facilities, and align ownership of land, infrastructure, and operations under a single entity.

points.point: Phase 1 mechanics: step-downs merge into DR Axion with no new shares, then DR Axion merges into Sunbeam after Sunbeam's equity is reorganised to Re 1 face value; Craftsman is not a party and its shareholding is unaffected. FY2025 turnover was Sunbeam INR1,237.46 crore (net worth 107.43) and DR Axion INR1,298.52 crore (net worth 511.34).
points.quote: After reorganization of the equity capital of the Amalgamated Company such that the face value of its equity shares is changed to INR 1/- each, issuance of 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of the Amalgamated Company having face value of INR 1/- (Indian Rupees One) each at a premium of INR 9/- (Indian Rupees Nine) each, for every 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of face value INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten) each held in the Amalgamating Company 3.

points.point: The simplification objective is stated separately from the growth case, covering managerial focus and operating efficiency.
points.quote: The proposed consolidation of DRA with Sunbeam is also expected to simplify the corporate structure and improve managerial focus and operational efficiency.

verdict.what_management_expects: One aluminium entity able to bid $100–200m orders toward $1bn scale; shared equipment, people and processes with one vendor code; Sunbeam's freed capacity reallocated as it exits legacy products (EBITDA ~7% to 10%+); unified land and asset ownership, stronger balance sheet, simpler structure. Margin gain only once capex matures and growth slows; said to fund investment, not deleverage; Craftsman's shareholding unchanged.
verdict.gaps: No valuation, listing, stake-sale or value-unlocking intent; no quantified cost or margin benefit; no timeline for moving Craftsman's own aluminium division; no tax or NCLT timeline.

verdict.segment_name: Aluminium Products (consolidated reportable segment; the entities under the Composite Scheme of Arrangement — DR Axion India, Suprash Developers and Srikara Technologies merging into Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions — sit inside this segment)
verdict.unit: ₹ lakhs for the annual segment tables; ₹ crore for the quarterly presentation figures
verdict.measure_notes: Operating profit = 'Segment Profit or Loss' as disclosed under Ind AS 108, i.e. segment EBIT before unallocable expenditure, other income, finance costs and exceptional items (not EBITDA, not PBT). Revenue is segment revenue that sums exactly to 'Total revenue as per Statement of Profit and Loss', so it is external revenue with no inter-segment figure disclosed. Figures taken on a consolidated basis because the entities in the Scheme are subsidiaries; standalone Aluminium Products segment figures are lower (FY2024 91,746 / 12,902; FY2025 1,15,957 / 11,600; FY2026 1,80,072 / 24,202 — AR2024 p93, AR2025 p172-173, AR2026 p165). The Scheme is an internal amalgamation of subsidiaries within this segment, not a separation/demerger with carve-out financials in these pages.

verdict.not_found: No segment-level PAT/net profit, tax, depreciation or EBITDA in any page; no standalone financials for Sunbeam, DR Axion, Suprash or Srikara as a separated business.

verdict.what_is_spun: Semiconductor business (fabless chip design, turnkey ASICs, power products); no demerger scheme appears in these documents.
verdict.reason: Carved out with a mandate to become India's first and largest fabless semiconductor company owning IP and delivering chips; given its own capital structure so Cyient shareholders are not penalised and independent value is established.
verdict.insiders: Cyient committed up to $100mn, about $30mn already invested; first external round dilutes only 10-12%, Cyient retains majority. Promoter and promoter group hold 24.70% of parent post-buyback and did not tender.
verdict.hidden_value: Semiconductors priced at $500mn ($4,650cr) post-money by EAAA while management says the parent's market attributes 'marginal, if not negative' value; still loss-making (H1 FY27 segment EBIT -Rs584mn), breakeven FY28; group non-current borrowings jumped to Rs22,506mn.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: No record date, entitlement ratio or listing stated; separation funded privately, so no index-exclusion or distributed-share overhang is on file.
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated as a listing date; on 26 May 2026 management said Cyient Semiconductors has 'long-term optionality that includes potentially a future spin-off path', and on 23 April 2026 the Board 'agreed in principle to explore a fundraise'. On 23 July 2026 a clean DLM demerger was declined.
verdict.read_next: Semiconductors segment EBIT and borrowings in the 22 Oct 2026 results, plus the omitted 3 March 2026 filing.
verdict.quote: Our goal is to build Cyient Semiconductors as a stand-alone business with its own governance, its own accountability and its own long-term optionality that includes potentially a future spin-off path.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is Cyient's global semiconductor arm, carved out effective 1 April 2025 into Cyient Semiconductors Private Limited (plus Singapore, US, UK, Germany, India and Cayman step-downs) with its own CEO (Suman Narayan), CFO (Ramya Mohan) and board, and reported from Q1 FY26 as a fourth segment alongside DET, DLM and Others, with DET restated to exclude it. Management's stated reason is twofold: the semiconductor model is capital-hungry in a way the engineering-services parent is not — Krishna Bodanapu drew an explicit parallel to Cyient DLM, saying 'the way semiconductor business works is more like a DLM kind of a structure where you do have a higher capital investment, you have design, which takes upfront capital' — and the losses from that investment were being punished inside the listed parent. The numbers they cited: semiconductor FY26 revenue of only $25.7M (Q4 $7.2M, +5% QoQ, fourth straight sequential rise) against a Q4 EBIT loss of $2.8M; group EBIT margin contracted 254bps YoY to 9.5% 'primarily reflecting strategic investments in the semiconductor business'; stated maximum organic investment of $15M, later a committed envelope of 'up to $100 million' of which ~$30M was deployed and ~$70M remained; breakeven slipping from FY27 to 'late FY27, early FY28' to FY28. The problem they said separation solves is valuation: Bodanapu argued the market ascribes 'marginal, if not negative' value to the unit because an EV/EBIT multiple on a loss-making business goes negative, that Cyient shareholders were 'getting penalized' for it, and that continuing to fund it from the parent without establishing its value was 'unfair to shareholders'; against that, turnkey ASIC companies 'have commanded valuation multiples nearly 3x those of semiconductor services firms', rising further with owned IP. The chosen mechanism was an independent capital structure rather than a demerger: Kinetic Technologies ($85M, 82.9% stake, ~250 products, 100+ patents, doubling addressable market to ~$8.5bn) was funded by ~$80M of low-cost Singapore-entity debt on the semiconductor balance sheet, and in May 2026 the unit signed its first external round with EAAA Alternatives (ex-Edelweiss Alternatives) — INR 300 crore as INR 200 crore debt plus INR 100 crore equity at an INR 4,650 crore / $500M post-money equity valuation, roughly 6–7x revenue — closed in Q1 FY27 as $30M of fresh capital. CFO Ramya Mohan framed the structure as giving 'a dedicated capital base', 'real operational discipline and financial separation from the parent', and 'its own long-term optionality that includes potentially a future spin-off path', with debt deliberately preferred over a large equity issue 'to protect it against dilution'. Management was explicit that a comparable clean demerger of Cyient DLM is not contemplated, because of engineering/manufacturing interdependence, and that an own capital structure is itself the value-unlock avenue.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced as a structural carve-out announced complete on the 24 Jul 2025 Q1 FY26 call (new four-segment reporting, DET restated ex-semis, start-up framing), and on 16 Oct 2025 Bodanapu first attached a valuation thesis to it — 'create a DLM like story for Cyient's shareholders' plus the 3x ASIC-vs-services multiple argument — while capping organic investment at $15M and promising EBIT-neutrality in FY27. Through 18 Dec 2025 (Kinetic signing) and 22 Jan 2026 the rationale shifted from services to an IP/product company needing sustained R&D, and Kinetic was financed on the subsidiary's own Singapore-entity debt rather than parent cash. On 23 Apr 2026 the Board agreed in principle to explore an external debt-and-equity raise 'for the semiconductor business, which is a stand-alone business and the step-down subsidiary', with Bodanapu naming the real driver — the market ascribes marginal-to-negative value and Cyient shareholders are being penalised — and guiding to only 10–12% initial dilution; by 26 May 2026 the EAAA deal was signed at a $500M post-money valuation with a 'potentially a future spin-off path' named for the first time, and on 23 Jul 2026 the $30M round was reported closed while a clean DLM demerger was declined on the same call.

points.point: Carve-out of the semiconductor business into a separate wholly owned subsidiary with its own leadership and reporting segment is announced as complete, with DET restated to exclude it and the unit framed as a start-up investment.
points.quote: Coming to the highlights for this quarter , It is my pleasure to announce that the Semiconductor business carve out process is completed as planned.

points.point: The unit is described as a separate subsidiary with its own leaders, management and structure, reported under a new four-segment structure (DET, DLM, Semiconductor, Others) precisely because its strategic plans differ.
points.quote: The reason why we've split it out as such is it has very different strategic plans.

points.point: Bodanapu gives the first explicit value-unlock rationale: replicate for shareholders what the separately capitalised, listed Cyient DLM did, including the stated $15M cap on organic investment and FY27 EBIT-neutrality.
points.quote: The opportunity here is to create a DLM like story for Cyient's shareholders through Cyient semiconductors.

points.point: The valuation arbitrage is quantified: turnkey ASIC and IP-owning businesses trade at multiples far above semiconductor services, which is why the unit must be valued on its own.
points.quote: Historically, turnkey ASIC companies have commanded valuation multiples nearly 3x those of semiconductor services firms, and as we gain ownership and control over IP, these multiples increase even further.

points.point: The Kinetic Technologies majority stake (~250 ASSP products, 100+ patents, doubling addressable market to $8.5bn) is justified by the need for sustained R&D and owned IP — the capital-intensity argument for a separate balance sheet.
points.quote: True product differentiation, scalable and profitable growth, and long -term shareholde r value in a semiconductor business is created through sustained investment in R&D, control of the semiconductor ecosystem for cost reduction, and the ownership of intellectual property and patents.

points.point: The Board agrees in principle to an external debt-and-equity fundraise, expressly ring-fenced to the stand-alone step-down subsidiary and driven by its growth and working-capital needs, alongside a INR 720 crore buyback at the parent.
points.quote: I just want to repeat that this is for the semiconductor business, which is a stand -alone business and the step -down subsidiary of Cyient Limited.

points.point: Asked to reconcile a parent buyback with a subsidiary fundraise, Bodanapu states the core problem the separation solves: Cyient shareholders are being penalised for semiconductor losses, so an independent valuation and capital structure is needed.
points.quote: So we want to make sure that the Cyient shareholders are not getting penalized for the performance of Cyient Semiconductor by establishing an independent valuation and an independent capital structure.

points.point: He quantifies the mispricing: on an EV/EBIT basis a loss-making unit carries marginal or negative value inside the listed parent, and funding it from Cyient without establishing value is unfair to shareholders (FY26 semi revenue $25.7M, Q4 EBIT -$2.8M).
points.quote: Now in terms of what percentage of Cyient's market cap now that's for our invest ors to determine, which as I understand it, the value that's attributed to Cyient Semiconductor is marginal, if not negative, because if we just do a simple EBIT multiple, EV to EBIT multiple, then it actually becomes negative because it's a money -losing business.

points.point: On the 26 May 2026 semiconductor financing call, CFO Ramya Mohan answers 'why raise external debt when there is cash with the parent' by naming financial separation, governance and a possible future spin-off as the goal — the clearest statement of intent on the separation.
points.quote: Our goal is to build Cyient Semiconduct ors as a stand -alone business with its own governance, its own accountability and its own long -term optionality that includes potentially a future spin -off path.

points.point: Bodanapu draws the explicit DLM parallel on capital intensity — upfront design capital — as the reason the unit needs its own capital structure and its own investor base, while keeping Cyient's up-to-$100M commitment ($30M already in, ~$70M available) intact.
points.quote: So, we think it's better that Cyient Semiconductor has its own independent capital structure with the kind of investors that want to participate in that capital structure, and we thought this was a good starting point.

points.point: The round is announced as INR 300 crore (INR 200 crore debt plus INR 100 crore equity) at an INR 4,650 crore / $500M post-money equity valuation from EAAA Alternatives, roughly 6–7x revenue, after inbound interest from global funds and strategics; debt was chosen over a large equity issue to limit dilution.
points.quote: But we made a deliberate choice not to issue a large amount of equity at this stage to protect it against dilution and preserve the shareholder value we are working to create.

points.point: The round is confirmed closed at $30M of fresh debt-and-equity capital at the $500M post-money valuation, framed as balance-sheet strength to fund the high-power ASSP development that is depressing operating profitability (breakeven now FY28, with ~$3M/quarter Kinetic amortisation).
points.quote: I am pleased to announce that we have closed this round $30 million of fresh capital raised through a combination of debt and equity is in place.

points.point: Asked by ChrysCapital for a clean DLM demerger to unlock value, Bodanapu declines on grounds of engineering/manufacturing interdependence and says the separate capital structure is itself the value-unlock avenue — defining the limits of the separation strategy.
points.quote: So we believe that the intent of establishing its own capital structure was to provide an avenue towards value unlock.

points.point: The FY26 audited results segment note records the legal restructuring: the global semiconductor business was reorganised under Cyient Semiconductors Private Limited effective 1 April 2025 and pulled out of the DET segment because that is how the CODM now reviews it.
points.quote: Effective April 01, 2025, the Group has reorganised its business structure by restructuring Its global semiconductor business under Cyient Semiconductors Private Limited, Its subsidiaries and an associate.

points.point: The Q2 FY27 filing shows the EAAA instruments landing on the subsidiary: Cyient Semiconductors Singapore issued INR 2,000Mn of 3-year NCDs and INR 1,000Mn of CCPS whose investor exit right forces liability (not equity) classification — evidence of an investor-protected, separable capital structure.
points.quote: The CCPS have fixed conversion terms and exit right on the Company if certain events do not occur within the stipulated period.

verdict.what_management_expects: For Cyient Semiconductors: dedicated long-cycle R&D capital, operational discipline and financial separation, ASSP gross margins of 50–60% versus services, EBIT breakeven in FY28, ASSP rising to 50–55% of mix, and an IP-led valuation (6–7x revenue, $500M) with optionality including a future spin-off. For Cyient: DET margins no longer dragged by semiconductor losses (group EBIT fell 254bps to 9.5%), no shareholder penalty, and value unlock via an independent, separately-funded structure.
verdict.gaps: No scheme of arrangement, demerger mechanics, record date, share-entitlement ratio, listing route or timetable for the stated spin-off path; no stranded-cost, tax or regulatory detail.

verdict.segment_name: Semiconductors (Semiconductors segment — Cyient Semiconductor Private Limited and its subsidiaries)
verdict.measure_notes: Operating profit = 'Segment results' per Ind AS 108 segment table (revenue less employee benefits, cost of materials, depreciation & amortisation and other expenses, net of allocable other income) — i.e. segment EBIT, before finance costs, exceptional items, unallocable income, share of associate loss and tax. Revenue is 'Revenue from contracts with customers' shown per segment; inter-segment revenue is eliminated only at the group total line, so segment revenue may include inter-segment amounts. Semiconductors became a separate reportable segment effective 1 April 2025; FY2025 is re-presented in AR2026. For the latest quarter the operating profit is EBIT from the quarterly 'Income Statement | Semiconductor' slide (EBITDA was -178 ₹Mn).

verdict.what_is_spun: not stated — the documents describe acquisitions (Swiss Parenterals 30% stake, Velbiom probiotics business), not a demerger
verdict.reason: not stated — no separation is disclosed; the stated objective is "fully consolidating its position, enhancing operational synergy, and strengthening its long-term strategic presence" by acquiring 100% of Swiss
verdict.insiders: No new entity disclosed. Mr. Naishadh Shah, Director of Swiss, allotted 23,06,372 Eris shares (1.69% fully diluted), locked in; no promoter/promoter group interest in the transaction
verdict.hidden_value: not stated. Documents disclose Swiss group turnover of Rs 220.80cr (FY23), Rs 282.97cr (FY24), Rs 351.11cr (FY25), presence in ~80+ countries, valued at Rs 423.30cr for 30%
verdict.selling_pressure_why: No demerger or share distribution in documents; only a locked-in preferential allotment of 1.69% to one acquiree
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated for any demerged entity; the 16 January 2026 filing says only "The aforesaid Subscription Shares shall be listed on the NSE and BSE, upon receipt of the relevant listing approvals"
verdict.read_next: Valuation report of Rashmi Shah dated 24 November 2025 supporting the Rs 423.30 crore Swiss consideration
verdict.quote: Pursuant to the said acquisition, Swiss will become a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.

verdict.rationale: These texts do not describe a separation, demerger or spin-off at all — they describe the opposite, a buy-in and full consolidation, so no separation rationale can be reconstructed from them. The only transaction explained is Eris Lifesciences' acquisition of the remaining 30% of Swiss Parenterals Limited (parenterals, incorporated 4 February 1997, presence in ~80+ countries) from Mr. Naishadh Shah, a Director of Swiss, taking Eris from 70% to 100% so that Swiss becomes a wholly owned subsidiary. The stated objects are 'fully consolidating its position, enhancing operational synergy, and strengthening its long-term strategic presence', with expected benefits of complete managerial control, full financial consolidation, improved cost efficiencies, streamlined governance and enhanced shareholder value. Consideration is INR 423.30 crore, discharged not in cash but by a preferential issue of up to 23,06,372 equity shares of face value Re. 1 at INR 1,835.35 each (premium INR 1,834.35), taking Mr. Shah from nil to 1.69% on a fully diluted basis, priced per Chapter V of the SEBI ICDR Regulations and a valuation report of 24 November 2025 by Rashmi Shah, Independent Registered Valuer (IBBI/RV/06/2018/10240). It is disclosed as a related party transaction (a transaction with a related party of a subsidiary under Regulation 2(zc) of SEBI LODR), stated to be at arm's length, with no promoter/promoter group/group company interest, no governmental or regulatory approvals required, and completion expected before 31 March 2026. The scale cited for Swiss is group-level turnover of INR 220.80 crore (FY2022-23), INR 282.97 crore (FY2023-24) and INR 351.11 crore (FY2024-25). No business is being carved out, no resulting entity is named, no demerger scheme or rationale clause is present, and no party (investor, lender or partner) is identified as having asked for anything.
verdict.evolution: No earnings call passages were supplied — the 'CALL PASSAGES' section is empty, so there is no call-by-call history to trace. The documentary trail runs only across two Regulation 30 intimations: the Board meeting of 24 November 2025 (2:45 PM to 5:30 PM) approving the 30% Swiss acquisition, the share-swap consideration and a postal ballot with a 21 November 2025 cut-off date; and the intimation of 16 January 2026 recording that shareholders approved by postal ballot on 24 December 2025 and that the Board's Executive Committee approved the allotment of the 23,06,372 shares that day. The plan therefore did not change over time in these texts — it moved from board approval to shareholder approval to allotment without alteration, and the filing explicitly records 'None' against any cancellation or termination of the issuance proposal.

points.point: The transaction is a consolidation, not a separation: Eris proposes to move from its existing 70% holding to 100% ownership of Swiss Parenterals, the stated purpose being consolidation of position, operational synergy and long-term strategic presence.
points.quote: With the objective of fully consolidating its position, enhancing operational synergy, and strengthening its long-term strategic presence, the Company now proposes to acquire 100% ownership of Swiss.

points.point: The benefits management lists are control, accounting and governance benefits rather than the focus/valuation arguments typical of a demerger rationale.
points.quote: This consolidation is expected to provide complete managerial control, enable full financial consolidation, improve cost efficiencies, streamline governance, and contribute to enhanced shareholder value.

points.point: End state of the deal: 16,74,493 Swiss shares (30% of its capital) are acquired and Swiss ceases to have a minority partner.
points.quote: Pursuant to the said acquisition, Swiss will become a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: Consideration of INR 423.30 crore is paid in Eris paper rather than cash, via a preferential allotment to the selling Swiss director Mr. Naishadh Shah at INR 1,835.35 per Re. 1 face value share, giving him 1.69% of Eris on a fully diluted basis.
points.quote: The acquisition of 30% stake in Swiss by the Company from Mr. Naishadh Shah is proposed to be undertaken for a total purchase consideration of INR 423,30,00,000 (Indian Rupees Four Hundred and Twenty Three Crores and Thirty Lakhs Only), which will be discharged by the Company by way of issuance of up to 23,06,372 (twenty three lakh six thousand three hundred and seventy two) equity shares of the Company on a preferential basis to Mr. Naishadh Shah

points.point: The deal is flagged as a material related party transaction because Mr. Shah is a Director of the subsidiary Swiss, requiring postal ballot approval; it is asserted to be at arm's length with no promoter interest.
points.quote: The transaction is being undertaken at arms' length.

points.point: Swiss's cited scale and reach: parenterals sold in roughly 80-plus countries, with group-level turnover rising from INR 220.80 crore in FY2022-23 to INR 282.97 crore in FY2023-24 and INR 351.11 crore in FY2024-25; no regulatory approval is needed and closing is targeted before 31 March 2026.
points.quote: Country in which the acquired entity has presence : ~80+ countries

points.point: The second filing (16 January 2026) confirms execution: shareholder consent by postal ballot on 24 December 2025 and allotment of the full 23,06,372 shares at a premium of INR 1,834.35 approved by the Executive Committee of the Board.
points.quote: the Executive Committee of the Board of the Directors of the Company at its meeting held today i.e., January 16, 2026 has approved the allotment of 23,06,372 (Twenty-Three Lakh Six Thousand Three Hundred and Seventy-Two) fully paid-up equity shares of face value of Re. 1 (Indian Rupee One) each

verdict.what_management_expects: Nothing is said about any separated entity, because none exists here. For Eris post-consolidation they expect complete managerial control, full financial consolidation of Swiss, improved cost efficiencies, streamlined governance, greater operational synergy, a stronger long-term strategic presence and enhanced shareholder value. verdict.rationale: The premise of a separation is not supported by these documents: the only structural transaction Lenskart has put before the exchanges is the opposite of a spin-off — a Scheme of Amalgamation (Board approved July 2, 2026, 141st Board meeting) folding two wholly-owned subsidiaries INTO the listed parent. Dealskart Online Services Private Limited (Transferor Company No. 1, turnover INR 6,247.71 Mn as on March 31, 2026), which provides operations-and-maintenance / manpower services, fixed-asset leasing and other ancillary services to Lenskart's omni-channel stores PAN India and was historically the master franchisee, and Lenskart Eyetech Private Limited (Transferor Company No. 2, turnover INR 312.39 Mn), which runs training centres for retail staff, both merge into Lenskart Solutions Limited (turnover INR 52,478.35 Mn) with Appointed Date April 1, 2026 under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013 before NCLT Delhi. The stated problems it solves are structural and administrative, not strategic: all three entities operate in the same eyewear/optical industry, so management says the businesses can be carried on 'more conveniently and advantageously', with multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances reduced, record-keeping streamlined, overheads and administrative/managerial expenditure cut, managerial, technical and financial resources pooled, and greater financial strength and flexibility achieved 'to maximize overall shareholder value'. Because both transferors are wholly-owned, no shares are issued, there is no change in the listed entity's shareholding pattern, Lenskart's own investment in them is cancelled, accounting follows the Pooling of Interest Method under Appendix C of Ind AS 103 (common control), and the transferors dissolve without winding up; the Scheme is also drawn to qualify as an 'amalgamation' under Section 2(6) of the Income Tax Act, 2025 so brought-forward tax losses and unabsorbed depreciation can be set off. No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for it: it is Board-initiated, exempt from a Stock Exchange No-Objection Letter under Regulation 37 read with the SEBI Master Circular of June 20, 2023, and filed only for disclosure. Two adjacent moves in the same window point the same direction — consolidation and backward integration rather than separation: at the same July 2, 2026 meeting the Board approved an 80:20 India JV with Mingfeng Glassesworld Limited, China ('Lenskart Metalframes Private Limited', paid-up capital INR 1,00,000) to manufacture metal spectacle frames and cut import dependence, and on February 11, 2026 it authorised converting pre-existing inter-company loans to equity in loss-making wholly-owned overseas subsidiaries Lenskart Singapore Pte. Ltd. and NESO Brands Pte. Ltd., which cannot service principal and interest.
verdict.evolution: Nothing resembling a separation surfaces in any of the three calls (Dec 1, 2025 for Q2 FY26; Feb 11, 2026 for Q3 FY26; May 20, 2026 for Q4/FY26) — no analyst asked and management never raised it. The only related thread is Dealskart's distorting effect on reported vs pro forma numbers, flagged in the Dec 2025 call, plus the Feb 11, 2026 Board's loan-to-equity conversions in Lenskart Singapore and NESO Brands; the structure question is answered only on July 2, 2026, when the Board approves amalgamation (not demerger) of Dealskart and Lenskart Eyetech with Appointed Date April 1, 2026. Direction of travel across the period is integration — Hyderabad plant, Thailand JV, the Mingfeng metal-frames JV — not separation.

points.point: The transaction is a consolidation, not a separation: two wholly-owned subsidiaries are absorbed into the listed parent to eliminate entities and put operations under one roof.
points.quote: In order to simplify and rationalize the group's corporate structure, the companies have undertaken the present Scheme with a view to streamlining the group's legal framework by eliminating multiple entities and consolidating the business operations under a single corporate entity.

points.point: The cited benefit is compliance and overhead cost reduction, not margin or valuation unlock.
points.quote: The proposed amalgamation will result in the simplification of the corporate structure by reducing the multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances, streamlining record-keeping, and generating cost efficiencies through the reduction of overheads and administrative, managerial, and other related expenditures;

points.point: Resource pooling and financial flexibility are the strategic claims, framed as shareholder-value maximisation and competitiveness.
points.quote: The proposed amalgamation will provide for pooling of the managerial, technical and financial resources of the Transferor Companies and the Transferee Company which will help in increasing the competitiveness of the Transferee Company;

points.point: No consideration moves and no shareholding changes, because both transferors are wholly owned; Lenskart's investment in them is simply cancelled.
points.quote: As Transferor Company No. 1 and Transferor Company No. 2 are wholly owned subsidiaries of Transferee Company, no shares will be issued in consideration of the merger.

points.point: Tax efficiency is explicit: the Scheme is built to Section 2(6) of the Income Tax Act, 2025 so losses and unabsorbed depreciation can be set off against the parent's profits.
points.quote: Further, brought forward tax losses and unabsorbed depreciation of the Transferor Companies in terms of the relevant provisions of the Income Tax Act, 2025 shall be allowable for set off against the profits of the Transferee Company subject to fulfillment of the conditions prescribed therein.

points.point: No stakeholder is said to have demanded it; the Board asserts the Scheme harms no constituency, and SEBI Regulation 37 exempts it from a Stock Exchange NOC, so it is filed only for disclosure.
points.quote: Further, there is no adverse effect of this Scheme on the directors, key management personnel, promoters, non-promoter members, creditors, and employees of the Companies and the same would be in the best interest of all stakeholders.

points.point: The only Dealskart discussion on any call is reporting hygiene: pre-consolidation B2B primary sales to the master franchisee distorted reported India growth (13% reported vs 22% pro forma).
points.quote: This disparity exists because in the last year Q2 numbers as per reported financials did not consolidate Dealskart and was higher than the actual secondary customer sales because of higher B2B primary sales between Lenskart and its master franchisee Dealskart ahead of the festive season stocking.

points.point: Management describes the franchise layer shrinking as a margin tailwind — consistent with absorbing the master-franchisee entity rather than separating it.
points.quote: Then in the other expenses, you also see incentives and commissions have been going down because as we are not adding new franchise stores, the relative share of the franchise commission expense keeps going down and that brings some operating leverage, right?

points.point: Earlier group-structure cleanup in the same direction: the Board authorised converting inter-company loans to equity in loss-making wholly-owned subsidiaries Lenskart Singapore and NESO Brands, which cannot service their debt.
points.quote: LK Singapore continues to be a loss-making entity. As it is unable to service the principal and interest obligations, it is proposed to convert the outstanding unsecured loan.

points.point: The same July 2, 2026 Board meeting approved an 80:20 India JV with Mingfeng Glassesworld (China) for metal spectacle frames — backward integration, the opposite of separating a business.
points.quote: The proposed Joint Venture will be engaged in the business of manufacturing metal spectacle frames in India with the objective of strengthening the Company's manufacturing capabilities, enhancing supply chain efficiencies, promoting localisation of manufacturing and reducing dependence on imports of metal frames.

points.point: Strategy articulated on the final call is deeper vertical integration and owning more of the value chain — no hint of carving anything out.
points.quote: Our ambition is to own even a greater share of the value chain now, from equipment to raw material to manufacturing, distribution, and the final mile to the customer, and then use AI to close the feedback loop across every layer of it.

verdict.insiders: Buyers "do not belong to the Promoter or Promoter Group of the Company"; transaction "would not fall within related party transactions". No promoter stake in buyer stated.

verdict.quote: As part of the Company’s strategy to divest it’s non-core assets, the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today i.e. July 11, 2026, has approved the divestment of 100% stake in Broadway, to AKRK Projects LLP and Partners and authorised for execution of Share Purchase Agreement.

verdict.rationale: Nothing in these texts describes a demerger, spin-off or NCLT scheme; what management actually explains are three narrower separations plus a new offshore holding vehicle. (1) The Consumer Healthcare/OTC business was carved out into a wholly-owned subsidiary of Mankind Pharma (announced on the Q2 FY25 call, first quarter of reporting as a separate segment in Q3 FY25) because OTC is a 'push' business whose channel economics and culture differ from prescription — Rajeev Juneja identified 'a mixed kind of a culture where one guy, one leader is taking care of OTC and pharma both' as the thing being fixed, alongside cutting stockist numbers from a few thousand, stopping cash-and-carry trade that was causing rate-cutting in the market, and pushing modern trade/e-commerce (9% of OTC sales in FY25 to 13% in FY26, growing 40–57%). (2) The numbers cited for OTC: INR232 cr (+20%) in Q2 FY25, INR193 cr (+30%) in Q3 FY25, INR809 cr (+15%) FY25, INR879 cr (+9%) FY26 with Q4 FY26 at INR213 cr (+20%); roughly 7% of company revenue at 18–20% EBITDA versus company guidance of 25–26%, which Abhishek Agarwal said is 'not going to contribute or significantly, you can say, dilute the overall margins.' (3) Separately, BSV's inherited TTK branded-generic prescription portfolio was separated out of BSV and slump-sold into Mankind (slump-sale notification flagged in Q1 FY26, transition effective 1 November 2025) on the logic that BSV should hold only super-specialty, high-entry-barrier biologics (Anti-D, Foligraf, HMG, ASVS, recombinants, immunoglobulins) while branded generics belong on Mankind's 'Delhi Mankind' platform, which 'understands the Rx business better.' (4) The TTK fix was quantified: three divisions collapsed into one, 600-plus field staff reduced to 440 by March 2025 and then ~325, MR productivity up from ~INR2 lakh PCPM to ~INR2.9 lakh, BSV blended PCPM 6.5 lakh versus above INR8 lakh excluding TTK, against TTK turnover that had collapsed from INR197 cr to INR104 cr (FY24 to FY25) after inventory corrections; total BSV synergies were guided at INR50–100 cr over 12–24 months, with margins 26–28% rising 50–100 bps a year toward 30% by FY30. Stamp duty on that intra-group slump sale was booked as an exceptional item in Q3 FY26, part of why reported EBITDA margin was 22.9% against adjusted 25.9%. (5) The third strand is non-core divestment to delever after the INR10,000 cr BSV debt raise: Mahananda Spa & Resorts sold for INR562 cr on 11 February 2025 (against a INR600–650 cr target for the two hospitality units), Broadway Hospitality Services approved for 100% sale to AKRK Projects LLP for INR49 cr on 11 July 2026 (FY26 revenue INR9.63 cr, 0.07% of company; net worth INR38.99 cr), BSV's surplus Hyderabad land being returned to the authorities with a INR13 cr impairment, and the dormant Sri Lanka subsidiary wound up on 13 April 2026. (6) No investor, lender or partner is recorded as asking for any of this: the demand side is management's own 'prudent financial strategy' and promoter long-termism, with shareholder-approved INR3,000 cr QIP proceeds, net debt down to INR3,932 cr and 1.1x adjusted EBITDA at Q4 FY26, and full acquisition-debt retirement targeted by FY28. (7) Forward-looking, the 11 July 2026 board also approved a Netherlands wholly-owned SPV (up to EUR 5 million) to hold R&D assets and do niche-therapy business development through JVs or strategic interests — i.e. ring-fencing innovation risk outside the operating company, alongside the Vadodara biotech plant funded via up to INR500 cr into Mankind Medicare, the manufacturing arm.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced on the Nov 2024 (Q2 FY25) call, where OTC was said to have been carved into a wholly-owned subsidiary for its 'next phase of growth' and, in the same breath, TTK was described as 'not a core BSV kind of a business' that 'will be separated out'; Ashutosh Dhawan simultaneously named Mahananda and Broadway as hospitality units being liquidated to retire debt. Jan 2025 reported the first post-carve-out OTC quarter (+30%) and explained the TTK shift as Mankind 'understanding the Rx business better'; May 2025 confirmed Mahananda's INR562 cr sale and framed the move as 'integration of BSV's prescription business into Mankind's platform'; Aug 2025 disclosed the formal slump-sale notification. Nov 2025 gave the field-force and PCPM metrics, Feb 2026 confirmed the 1 November 2025 transition, the stamp-duty exceptional and the Hyderabad land impairment, and May 2026 moved on to the Vadodara biotech build via Mankind Medicare. The filings then extend the same non-core logic: Sri Lanka WOS wound up 13 April 2026, and on 11 July 2026 Broadway sold for INR49 cr while a Netherlands R&D SPV was approved — so the plan migrated from fixing acquired businesses to housing new R&D risk offshore.

points.point: First announcement of the OTC/Consumer Healthcare carve-out into a wholly-owned subsidiary, justified purely on the business's untapped potential; OTC revenue that quarter was INR232 cr, up 20% YoY.
points.quote: We believe this business has a huge potential, and hence, we have carved out our OTC business to a wholly owned subsidiary of Mankind Pharma, which sets this business for next phase of growth.

points.point: On the same call Rajeev Juneja said BSV's inherited TTK prescription business was not core to BSV and would be separated out, and that Mankind's arrival would accelerate everything else at BSV.
points.quote: TTK business will come, which is not a core BSV kind of a business, will be separated out - I mean, the right things will happen.

points.point: The non-core divestment track was set out at the same time: two hospitality units (Mahananda and Broadway) were already in liquidation, targeted at INR600–650 cr of proceeds explicitly earmarked for repaying the INR10,000 cr BSV acquisition debt.
points.quote: So these are the two hospitality units, one is the name of Mahananda, separate entity and one is broadway which are in the process of being liquidated.

points.point: Management mapped the overlap it expected between BSV and Mankind at only 5–10%, with TTK the single place needing restructuring because its 3–4 divisions sold branded prescription products that belong on Mankind's Delhi platform.
points.quote: We see 5 - 10% overlapping that's all, nothing more.

points.point: First quarter of OTC operating as a separate subsidiary, framed as unlocking its 'true potential'; revenue rose 30% YoY to INR193 cr in Q3 FY25 and 15% to INR631 cr for 9M FY25.
points.quote: This has been the first quarter of the OTC business post carving out the same into wholly-owned subsidiary of Mankind to maximize its true potential.

points.point: Rajeev Juneja gave the clearest statement of the problem the OTC separation solves — one leader running both OTC and pharma produced a mixed culture, alongside too many distributors; growth followed the split.
points.quote: I mean, it was number of distributors, whether hiving off, bringing different talent, making sure that it's not a mixed kind of a culture where one guy, one leader is taking care of OTC and pharma both.

points.point: Prakash Agarwal explained the TTK/Rx shift as a capability argument plus field-force and portfolio rationalisation: a very small division carrying more than 600 people, with hygiene of the business as the stated goal.
points.quote: So there is a significant restructuring going in the Rx business, that is the TTK business of the BSV. Because we understand Rx business better, that is getting shifted to Mankind.

points.point: The structural logic was spelled out: TTK's branded prescription brands sit naturally in Delhi Mankind, while BSV retains only super-specialty, high-entry-barrier products; by March 2025 TTK's three divisions were one and headcount had gone from 600+ to 440.
points.quote: When we acquired BSV, it came to us with TTK products - prescription brands, which we have integrated in Mankind because for that, Delhi Mankind is an appropriate company.

points.point: Completion of the first non-core separation was confirmed, with proceeds recycled into deleveraging and the accounts split into continuing and discontinued operations.
points.quote: Also, as committed, we have monetized our noncore asset that is Mahananda Spa and Resorts Private Limited for a cash consideration of INR562 crores on 11th of February 2025.

points.point: The TTK transfer was formalised as a slump sale, with Mankind's office to run it entirely because it is a branded-generic business; Rajeev Juneja listed it among promises delivered, alongside the QIP, the Mahananda sale and the new biologics plant.
points.quote: Actually, some growth is there. We are not calling out the number, but there is some growth, especially in the international business and also in the specialty.

points.point: Rajeev Juneja presented the TTK shift to Mankind as one of a checklist of structural commitments already executed — QIP, hotel sale, TTK transfer, second biologics plant, R&D expansion.
points.quote: We said that TTK prescription business will be shifted to Mankind. It has been done.

points.point: Quantified the synergy from separating TTK onto Mankind's operating model: field force normalised from 550-plus MRs to about 325 with productivity up roughly 45%, described as the one big synergy already played out, plus vendor/raw-material renegotiation.
points.quote: So from 550-plus MRs that has been normalized to about 325 plus. Sales have started improving. We are seeing MR productivity increase from around INR2 lakh PCPM to now about INR2.9 lakh PCPM and we expect this number to grow much more in the upcoming quarters and years.

points.point: The intra-group slump sale took effect 1 November 2025 and the restructured prescription portfolio had already beaten full-year FY25 sales within nine months of FY26.
points.quote: The restructured prescription portfolio which transitioned to Mankind effective 1st of November 2025 has performed really well.

points.point: The cost of the separation showed up in reported numbers: stamp duty on the BSV branded-generic slump sale plus surplus-asset impairment cut reported EBITDA margin to 22.9% against 25.9% adjusted.
points.quote: This decrease is attributable to exceptional items comprising of New Labour Code adoption, stamp duty on slump sale of BSV branded generic business within the group, and impairment of some noncurrent surplus assets.

points.point: A further asset separation was disclosed — BSV's Hyderabad land reclassified as surplus and being returned to the authorities because manufacturing is consolidating at Vadodara, with a INR13 cr impairment taken.
points.quote: And since we are building up the facility at Vadodara. So therefore, this particular piece of land has been classified as a surplus land. So therefore, we are in the process of returning it back to the authorities, this land.

points.point: Manufacturing and biotech capacity is being concentrated in a separate subsidiary vehicle, with up to INR500 cr approved into Mankind Medicare entirely for the Vadodara biotech facility; FY27 capex guided up to 6–7% of revenue.
points.quote: So Medicare is basically the manufacturing arm of Mankind. So this investment is towards setting up of best-in-class Vadodara biotech facility.

points.point: Filing of 11 July 2026: board approved 100% divestment of Broadway Hospitality Services to AKRK Projects LLP (not promoter-related, not a related-party transaction) for INR49 cr, closing within 90 days; Broadway contributed INR9.63 cr revenue (0.07%) and INR38.99 cr net worth in FY26.
points.quote: As part of the Company’s strategy to divest it’s non-core assets, the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today i.e. July 11, 2026, has approved the divestment of 100% stake in Broadway, to AKRK Projects LLP and Partners and authorised for execution of Share Purchase Agreement.

points.point: The same 11 July 2026 board approved a Netherlands wholly-owned SPV, funded up to EUR 5 million in tranches, to ring-fence R&D asset holdings and niche-therapy business development outside the operating company.
points.quote: The new company would be operating in the capacity of holding investments in R&D assets and carrying out business development activities focused on treatment of niche therapies, either through joint venture or acquiring strategic interests, as the opportunities arises.

points.point: Filing of 13 April 2026: the dormant Sri Lankan wholly-owned subsidiary was wound up because regulatory change made its business objectives unviable; it had no operations and was not a material subsidiary.
points.quote: the Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held today, has approved the closure/winding-up of Mankind Pharma Lanka (Private) Limited (“WOS”), a wholly owned subsidiary company incorporated in Sri Lanka, as due to changed regulatory requirements, the anticipated business objectives are no longer viable.

verdict.what_management_expects: OTC subsidiary: own leadership and culture, cleaner channel (stockists cut, cash-and-carry stopped, e-com/MT 9%→13%), double-digit growth, 18–20% EBITDA scaling to company average. BSV: retains only super-specialty high-entry-barrier biologics, 26–28% margins rising 50–100 bps yearly toward 30%. Mankind: TTK branded generics on its Rx platform, PCPM INR2→2.9 lakh, INR50–100 cr synergies. Divestments fund deleveraging to 1.1x, debt-free by FY28.
verdict.gaps: No demerger scheme, listing, shareholder entitlement or valuation-unlock case; no separate OTC subsidiary financials; no slump-sale consideration, tax or stamp-duty quantum; no investor, lender or partner demand named.

verdict.what_is_spun: Tata Motors' commercial vehicle business — trucks, buses, vans, pick-ups — demerged into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited, now listed separately
demerged_business_names: Tata Motors Limited (formerly TML Commercial Vehicles Limited)
verdict.reason: not stated; filings only describe the outcome — CFO says demerger effective 1 October 2025 makes Tata Motors "a pure play commercial vehicle company"; no rationale given in these documents
verdict.insiders: Promoter/management stake not stated. Incentives: TML Share-based Long Term Incentive Scheme approved 11 March 2026 — up to 23,07,647 shares (0.062% dilution), PSUs at Rs 2 exercise price, replacing demerged company PSUs 1:1
verdict.hidden_value: A pure-play CV company with standalone FY26 revenue ~Rs 77,000 cr, EBITDA margin 13.2% (7.8% in FY23), EBIT 11%, FCF Rs 9,200 cr (12% of revenue), ROCE 72%, net cash Rs 7,500 cr — now levering up for Iveco (EUR 3,825,000,000 facility)
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Documents give listing dates only; no share-entitlement size, shareholder base or index inclusion/exclusion detail stated
verdict.listing_timeline: Demerger "effective from 1st of October 2025"; name changed "to Tata Motors Limited from TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (effective 29 October 2025)"; "equity shares have been listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited, effective 12th November 2025" (stated in press releases of 1 February 2026, 1 March 2026 and 1 April 2026)
verdict.read_next: The NCLT-sanctioned Composite Scheme of Arrangement — share-entitlement ratio and promoter shareholding in the resulting company
verdict.quote: Demerger being effective from 1 st of October 2025, Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company, and this is a defining shift that changes how we think is most appropriate to present our financials.

verdict.rationale: Management presents the separation as a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232, sanctioned by the NCLT Mumbai Bench amongst Tata Motors Limited (the demerged company, now Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited), TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (the resulting company) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (amalgamated into the demerged entity), effective 1 October 2025; the resulting company was renamed Tata Motors Limited on 29 October 2025 and its shares listed on BSE/NSE (ticker TMCV) on 12 November 2025, with outstanding PSUs replaced one-for-one under a new scheme covering up to 23,07,647 shares (0.062% dilution). The stated problem the split solves is a reporting and identity one: 'Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then' — from Q4 FY26 the company reports standalone financials including the Tata Cummins joint operation as its primary lens, giving 'a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture'. The separation cost ₹960 crore of one-time demerger expense booked in Q3 FY26 (part of ₹1,500 crore standalone / ₹1,600 crore consolidated exceptionals, alongside ₹603 crore of new labour code and ₹82 crore of Iveco acquisition cost). The pure-play case is argued with numbers: FY26 revenue ₹77,000 crore (vs ₹66,000 crore FY23), EBITDA margin up from 7.8% (FY23) to 13.2% (FY26) — ~550bps of 'structural improvement' — EBITDA doubled from ₹5,100 crore to ₹10,200 crore, PBT before exceptionals ₹8,700 crore, first-ever double-digit EBIT at 11% (the CV segment first crossed it at 10.6% in Q3 FY26), FCF ₹9,200 crore or 12% of revenue, Auto ROCE 72%, cash conversion cycle of negative 31 days, net cash ₹7,500 crore standalone and ₹13,700 crore consolidated, and a maiden final dividend of ₹4/share (~₹1,500 crore outflow). Cyclicality is the second problem: non-cyclical revenue (parts & service, Fleet Edge digital subscriptions, Smart City e-bus operations) is compounding at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR, 'deliberately building this mix', and Q4 working-capital sinks historically concentrated in Q4 have been spread through the year. Third, the standalone CV entity became the acquisition vehicle: its own balance sheet and a committed EUR 3.825 billion bridge from Morgan Stanley and MUFG funded an all-cash voluntary totalitarian tender offer for Iveco Group N.V. at EUR 14.10 (raised to EUR 14.40), valuing Iveco at ~EUR 3.82 billion, creating ~EUR 21 billion (INR 2,28,000 crore+) of combined revenue and ~590k units with Europe ~46%/India ~32%/South America ~8%/RoW ~14% and 'substantially no overlap' — expected to 'drive better operating leverage by spreading its capital investments over larger volumes, generating operating efficiencies and reducing the cash flow volatility inherent in the commercial vehicles sector', plus enhancing Iveco's FPT powertrain business. Structural simplification continues inside the CV entity: TMF Holdings Limited and TMF Business Services Limited (wholly owned subsidiaries) are being amalgamated into it, and Tata Motor Finance had already been folded into Tata Capital (whose October 2025 IPO priced 20–25% below the merger valuation, forcing a ₹2,000 crore mark-to-market loss in Q2 FY26 and a ₹295 crore write-back in Q3).
verdict.evolution: In the Nov 2025 call (Q2 FY26, 13 November 2025) management reported the split as done rather than argued for it — demerger effective 1 October, CV listing completed as TMCV 'as committed previously', Iveco approvals underway and the bridge loan secured. In the Feb 2026 call (Q3 FY26, 29 January 2026) the cost showed up as a ₹960 crore one-time demerger exceptional while the CV segment hit a double-digit EBIT margin (10.6%) for the first time and Iveco approvals were guided to end-March. In the May 2026 call (Q4 FY26, 13 May 2026) the framing shifted decisively: 'Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company... a defining shift', the old carved-out CV segment was retired in favour of standalone reporting, three-year pure-play metrics were laid out, and Iveco closure slipped to Q2 FY27 pending French and Spanish financial-regulator approvals. Filings then show execution: offer launched 4 September 2026, 89.42% tendered by 27 October 2026, 96.29% after the reopening on 6 November 2026, triggering the Dutch legal squeeze-out, alongside the TMF Holdings/TMF Business Services amalgamation notices.

verdict.rationale: The separation is the demerger of the power-evacuation / substation (common infrastructure) business out of Inox Wind's listed O&M subsidiary Inox Green Energy Services Ltd (IGESL, ~56% held by IWL, later diluted to 54.78%) and its merger into Inox Renewable Solutions Ltd (IRSL, formerly Resco Global Wind Services, ~88.84% held by IWL), IWL's EPC arm, after which IRSL is automatically listed and Inox Green's shareholders receive 122 IRSL shares for every 1,000 Inox Green shares. The problem management says it fixes: Inox Green's balance sheet carried roughly Rs 1,000 crore of gross block of substations/evacuation assets (84 substations pan-India) that produced only about Rs 10 crore of revenue but around Rs 50-55 crore of annual depreciation, depressing PBT, ROE and ROCE and burying the asset-light ~50%-EBITDA-margin O&M business. Post-demerger Inox Green has virtually no depreciation and negligible finance cost, so PBT equals EBITDA equals cash profit — FY27 EBITDA guided above Rs 600 crore, 'broadly everything' converting to operating cash profit, helped by a ~Rs 700 crore accumulated-loss tax shield. The infrastructure instead lands in IRSL, where the group's EPC capability, in-housed cranes, transformer manufacturing and multi-gigawatt project/land pipeline already sit, and whose value rose after the Sept-2025 CERC amendment allowing hybridisation of existing wind evacuation with solar above 50 MW — giving access to what Devansh Jain called almost 10 GW of plug-and-play infrastructure. Akhil Jindal framed the intent as shareholder choice: investors can hold the O&M business, the infrastructure business, or the whole value chain through Inox Wind, and he said no further corporate action is therefore needed (explicitly refusing to demerge Green or IRSL out of IWL). Value-unlocking is the other stated driver: IRSL raised Rs 175 crore in Sept 2025 at a valuation of ~Rs 7,400 crore, and IWL has since sold small IRSL stakes to group parties (91.90%→88.84% for Rs 173.5 crore; then →87.98% for ~Rs 50 crore). Investors and analysts (Vishal Singh, Pradyumna Choudhary, Hansal Thakker, Prit Nagersheth, Pradeep Motwani) repeatedly pressed on timing and on whether minority shareholders would see value unlocked; the scheme also required and received approval from equity shareholders, warrant holders and secured and unsecured creditors (1 Nov 2025) — no lender or partner demand was cited as the trigger.
verdict.evolution: IGESL's board approved the scheme on 13 Nov 2024; the earliest discussion in these transcripts is the Feb 2025 call (31 Jan 2025), where Manish Garg confirmed board approval and filing with NSE/BSE after an investor asked when 'the demerger of that EPC subsidiary' would happen. By the Sep 2025 call (1 Sep 2025) exchange no-objections were in, the scheme was filed at NCLT Ahmedabad with approval guided in 2-3 quarters, IRSL had raised Rs 175 crore at ~Rs 7,400 crore, and Akhil Jindal reframed the logic as giving shareholders a choice of which business to own while ruling out any further demerger out of IWL. On the Nov 2025 call (14 Nov 2025) shareholder and creditor approvals were announced and Devansh Jain said the demerger and IRSL listing would 'unlock substantial value'; on the Feb 2026 call (13 Feb 2026) it was in final NCLT hearings with the impact quantified (only ~Rs 10 crore revenue out, ~Rs 50 crore depreciation out, 84 substations to be merged). NCLT sanctioned it on 12 March 2026, effective 4 May 2026, and on the Jun 2026 call (29 May 2026) management confirmed the Rs 1,000 crore gross block and Rs 50-55 crore depreciation were eliminated, with listing 1-2 months away, while declining to give IRSL's financials until it is demerged.

points.point: First disclosure in these calls: the IGESL board had approved demerging the substation business and the scheme was filed with NSE/BSE, to be followed by an NCLT filing; an investor had asked when the 'EPC subsidiary' demerger would happen.
points.quote: So the Board approval for a demerger of the substation business from Inox Green has already been taken in the last Board meeting, the scheme has been filed with NSE and BSE, and we are waiting for their approval.

points.point: Akhil Jindal explained the mechanics — infrastructure and connectivity assets move out of Inox Green into Resco/IRSL, which then lists automatically, with Inox Green shareholders receiving IRSL shares.
points.quote: Under that, there would have been an automatic listing of Resco. And to that extent, the shareholders of INOX Green would be getting the shares of INOX Resco also.

points.point: Asked whether IGESL and IRSL would later be demerged to IWL shareholders, Jindal said the point of separating these businesses was to let shareholders pick which business to own, so no further corporate action is needed.
points.quote: As management, we have provided enough window for a shareholder to be present where he wants to be. And I think that was the intention of separating these businesses.

points.point: The balance-sheet rationale quantified: ~Rs 1,000 crore gross block leaves Inox Green and ~Rs 50-55 crore of annual depreciation is eliminated, lifting PBT and improving ROE/ROCE.
points.quote: Once the scheme is approved by the NCLT, the gross block of around INR1,000 crores will be off our balance sheet and subsequently the depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores annually will be eliminated, thereby increasing the PBT by that amount.

points.point: IRSL was independently valued shortly before the demerger, and the CERC hybridisation amendment (allowing existing wind evacuation infra to be shared with solar above 50 MW) multiplied the value of the infrastructure being moved into it.
points.quote: We have recently raised INR175 crores at Inox Renewable Solutions at a valuation of approximately INR7,400 crores.

points.point: Devansh Jain sized the infrastructure asset that IRSL will house post-hybridisation as near-unique in India.
points.quote: I think it gives us access to almost 10 gigawatts of plug and play infrastructure across wind and solar , which is huge.

points.point: On receiving shareholder and creditor approvals, Sanjeev Agarwal set out the two-sided benefit: IRSL lists as Inox Wind's EPC arm, Inox Green sheds the depreciation on the demerged asset blocks.
points.quote: This will add value for both Inox Wind, with subsequent listing of Inox Renewable solution as an EPC arm of Inox Wind, and Inox Green with elimination of depreciation on demergers of the asset blocks

points.point: Devansh Jain stated the headline objective as value unlocking for both listed entities.
points.quote: I believe that the de-merger and subsequent listing of Inox Renewable Solutions will unlock substantial value for both Inox Wind and Inox Green.

points.point: Management quantified the asymmetry that makes the separation accretive for Inox Green: barely any revenue leaves, but the depreciation does.
points.quote: So post the demerger, as we have clarified on the multiple cores, there would be a very limited amount of revenue in the range of INR 10 odd crore will get out of the balance sheet. And around INR 50 odd crores of depreciation will go out from the balance sheet.

points.point: Mathusudhana described the scale of the infrastructure being consolidated — 84 substations pan-India — and claimed further unquantified synergy value plus a connectivity advantage no competitor has.
points.quote: And like merging 84 substations across India, it will be a huge exercise. And that will unlock synergy value, which we will reveal in the future.

points.point: Post-NCLT confirmation that the benefit has crystallised in Inox Green's accounts, with the residual step being administrative before IRSL's automatic listing (guided at 1-2 months).
points.quote: With this gross block of approximately INR1,000 crores has been eliminated from Inox Green's balance sheet. And subsequently, the annual depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores has been eliminated, thereby increasing the profitability.

points.point: Devansh Jain placed the IRSL demerger in a sequence of value-creating separations, after the Inox Green spin-off, while shrugging off the share-price criticism from minority holders.
points.quote: We've spun off Inox Green, which has created tremendous value. We're on the verge of demerging Inox Renewable Solutions, which we hope will create tremendous value.

points.point: Management refused to give any top-line or EBITDA profile for the business being separated until the demerger is complete.
points.quote: We cannot say at this point in time. I think once that demerged, we'll elucidate more plans. At this point in time, it's part and parcel of Inox Wind.

points.point: Post-demerger Inox Green is positioned as a near-pure cash generator: no depreciation, no finance cost and a ~Rs 700 crore loss tax shield, with FY27 EBITDA guided above Rs 600 crore.
points.quote: Out of INR600 crore fees, broadly everything will be converted into the operating cash flow. As such, there will be no depreciation, no finance cost, and we have a tax shield up to INR700 crore of losses.

points.point: The filings record the legal path: IGESL board approval 13 Nov 2024 for demerger of the Power Evacuation business into IRSL under sections 230-232; approval by equity shareholders, warrant holders and secured and unsecured creditors on 1 Nov 2025; NCLT Ahmedabad sanction on 12 March 2026; effective 4 May 2026.
points.quote: On March, 12, 2026, Hon'ble National Company law Tribunal, Ahmedabad (NCLT) sanctioned the Scheme.

points.quote: Pursuant to the Scheme, 122 equity share in the Resulting company for every 1000 share held in the demerged company to be issued to the shareholders as on the record date.

points.point: The demerger itself reduces Inox Wind's holding in IRSL, though control is retained under Ind AS 110.
points.quote: Furhter, due to effect of the demerger scheme between the lnox Renewable Solutions Limited and lnox Green Energy Services Limited as approved by NCLT vide order dated 13 March 2026, the Company shareholding in IRSL is expected to reduced from 88.41% to 79.75%.

verdict.what_management_expects: Inox Green: ~Rs 1,000 cr gross block and ~Rs 50-55 cr annual depreciation gone, higher PBT, sharply better ROE/ROCE, a pure-play ~50%-margin asset-light O&M business whose FY27 EBITDA (>Rs 600 cr) converts almost fully to cash. IRSL: a separately listed EPC/infrastructure arm of Inox Wind holding evacuation infra, cranes, transformers and hybridisation-ready plug-and-play sites. Both: substantial value unlocking.
verdict.gaps: No IRSL standalone revenue, EBITDA, debt or valuation basis disclosed; no explanation of the 122:1,000 share ratio, tax treatment, IRSL's post-listing capital needs, or any lender requirement.
